title.rendered: How to Use Front and Back Cameras at the Same Time on iPhone

content.rendered:
Want to record yourself and what’s in front of you at the same time without editing split screens later? Whether you’re shooting a vlog, recording an interview, or capturing a live event reaction, switching between cameras can be frustrating.

The good news is that you can use both the front and back cameras on your iPhone simultaneously. In this guide, I’ll show you the easiest ways to do it, with and without third-party apps.

Table of Contents
  • Method 1: Use Dual Capture Mode in the iPhone Camera App (iPhone 17 Series)
  • Method 2: Use Third-Party Apps to Record With Both iPhone Cameras
  • Method 3: Use Dual Camera Mode in Social Media Apps
    • Use Dual Camera Mode on Instagram
    • Record With Dual Camera on Snapchat
  • Tips for Recording Better Videos With Both iPhone Cameras
  • Final Words

Method 1: Use Dual Capture Mode in the iPhone Camera App (iPhone 17 Series)

If you’re using an iPhone 17 series model, Apple includes a built-in Dual Capture mode inside the Camera app. This is the simplest and most convenient method since you don’t need to install anything. Here’s how to use it:

  1. Open the Camera app and swipe to Video mode.
  2. Tap the three-dots button in the top-right corner and select Dual Capture.
  3. Tap the Record button to start recording.
  4. Tap Stop when you’re done. Your video will be saved as a single file that combines both front and rear camera views.

Dual Capture mode is useful for instant dual-camera recording, but it still has some limitations. It currently works only on iPhone 17 models and offers just one fixed layout, with no picture-in-picture, split-screen, or other customization options. It also cannot record at 60 or 120 fps, even though the iPhone 17 supports those frame rates.

Method 2: Use Third-Party Apps to Record With Both iPhone Cameras

If your iPhone doesn’t support built-in dual capture or you want more customization options, you can use a third-party app like Dualgram.

Dualgram is a free app that gives you more control over layouts and output quality. For example, you can manually select the audio output channel, take photos while recording, choose from more than six layouts, zoom in and out, and more. Overall, it’s one of the best apps for recording with both cameras at the same time.

Use Dualgram to Record With Front and Rear Cameras:

  1. Install Dualgram from the App Store.
  2. Open the app and allow camera and microphone permissions.
  3. Choose your preferred layout and settings.
  4. Tap the Record button.
  5. Tap Stop to save the video.

The app will export a combined video file that you can edit or upload anywhere.

Alternative apps to try

If Dualgram doesn’t meet your needs, you can also try:

  • 2Camera Dual Camera Front Back: This app provides a custom UI, advanced controls, multiple lens layout options, and more. If you want greater control over the camera, this app is worth trying.
  • MixCam: User reviews suggest the app is very easy to use and offers features such as real-time motion blur in video, photocard support, and emojis.

Each app offers different layouts and export options, so choose based on how much control you want.

Method 3: Use Dual Camera Mode in Social Media Apps

Many social media apps now support dual-camera recording directly inside the app. This is perfect if you mainly create content for social platforms and want a quick option without installing extra apps.

Use Dual Camera Mode on Instagram

  1. Open Instagram.
  2. Go to Story or Reels.
  3. Tap down arrow on the left.
  4. Choose Dual from camera modes.
  5. Frame your shot and tap the Record button.

Instagram records the video and saves it to your drafts or stories.

Record With Dual Camera on Snapchat

  1. Open Snapchat.
  2. Tap Dual Camera under the arrow on the right side of the screen.
  3. You can also select a preferred layout: Horizontal, Vertical, or Picture-in-Picture.
  4. Hold the Capture button to record.

You can post it directly to your Story, send it to friends, or save it to Memories.

Tips for Recording Better Videos With Both iPhone Cameras

Here are a few tips to help you get better results when recording with both cameras simultaneously:

  • Adjust composition carefully: The rear camera is usually the primary view, while the front camera appears as a smaller overlay. Frame your subject in the main view before recording.
  • Use good lighting: Both lenses need proper lighting for clear footage.
  • Stabilize your iPhone: Use Action mode, a tripod, or a MagSafe mount to avoid shaky video.
  • Manage storage space: Dual recording uses more storage. As a rule of thumb, keep around 5 minutes of free storage for every 1 minute of video to avoid issues.
  • Use an external microphone: Built-in microphones are good, but they may not capture clear audio in noisy environments.
  • Record reactions or reviews: Use a split-screen layout to show the product or scene while keeping your face visible for reactions.
  • Record vlogs or travel content: Capture the scenery with the rear camera while using the front camera for narration.

These small adjustments can make a big difference in video quality.

Final Words

Using both the front and back cameras on your iPhone is easier than most people think. If you have an iPhone 17 series model, the built-in Dual Capture mode is the simplest solution. For older models, apps like Dualgram, MixCam, or even social media features like Instagram’s Dual mode work well.

This setup is perfect for vlogs, tutorials, interviews, reaction videos, and storytelling. Once you try it, you’ll likely find plenty of creative ways to use it.

FAQs

Can all iPhones record with both front and rear cameras simultaneously?

No. Built-in dual recording is available only on newer models such as the iPhone 17 series. Older iPhones require third-party apps.

Does dual-camera recording reduce video quality?

It may limit resolution or frame rate depending on the method or app you use.

Does dual recording drain the battery faster?

Yes. Since both cameras and processing units are active, battery usage increases.

Can I edit each camera view separately later?

Most apps combine both feeds into a single video file. Some professional apps may offer more advanced editing options.

blockGraphs.answer: No. Built-in dual recording is available only on newer models such as the iPhone 17 series. Older iPhones require third-party apps.

blockGraphs.question: Does dual-camera recording reduce video quality?
blockGraphs.answer: It may limit resolution or frame rate depending on the method or app you use.

blockGraphs.question: Does dual recording drain the battery faster?
blockGraphs.answer: Yes. Since both cameras and processing units are active, battery usage increases.

blockGraphs.question: Can I edit each camera view separately later?
blockGraphs.answer: Most apps combine both feeds into a single video file. Some professional apps may offer more advanced editing options.

title.rendered: Purported iPhone Fold CAD Files Reveal Apple’s Foldable iPhone Design

content.rendered:
Apple’s first foldable iPhone may have appeared in early design files shared publicly. Images of what are described as 3D CAD rendering files show a device with a foldable form factor, a dual‑camera rear system, and a hinge-based design that shapes the device’s exterior when closed.

The CAD files surfaced in images released by Sonny Dickson, a long‑time collector of unreleased Apple hardware prototypes and design materials. The images show the rear of the device and the layout of the phone when opened, offering a look at how Apple may be approaching the design of a foldable iPhone.

Rear Design Shows Dual Cameras on Raised Plateau

The files depict a camera module that resembles the raised plateau design used on Apple’s thinner iPhone Air hardware. Unlike that device, however, the foldable model appears to include two rear cameras rather than a single lens. The model as previously rumoured looks more like an iPad when unfolded.

pic.twitter.com/p0x5T1G1DH

— Sonny Dickson (@SonnyDickson) March 9, 2026

The module sits across the back panel in a horizontal plateau that slightly elevates the camera hardware from the rest of the device. This layout suggests Apple may be prioritizing a slimmer folded body while still accommodating multiple cameras.

Hinge Placement Shapes the Device’s Corners

The CAD images show an unusual exterior shape. Two corners of the device appear rounded, while the opposite side features squared edges where the hinge mechanism would be located.

This combination indicates the hinge occupies a defined structural area along one side of the device. When folded, that hinge section would form the squared edge of the phone, while the opposite side maintains the more typical curved corner design seen on recent iPhones.

Open Layout Reveals Internal Display Camera Position

One image shows the phone in its unfolded state. The internal display appears to include a small circular cutout near the top-left corner, which likely houses the front-facing camera used when the device is opened like a tablet.

The design files also outline the outer edges of the device in both open and closed configurations, including the placement of the outer display that would be visible when the phone is folded shut.

CAD Files Appear During Typical Pre‑Launch Window

Design files for upcoming iPhone hardware commonly begin circulating months before release as accessory makers prepare cases and other hardware. CAD models allow those manufacturers to design products that match the dimensions and hardware placement of unreleased devices.

The details shown in the images broadly align with previously described hardware expectations for Apple’s foldable iPhone, including a book-style folding mechanism and a dual‑camera rear system.

Apple has not publicly confirmed plans for a foldable iPhone or announced any product with this design.

title.rendered: iPhone 17e vs Google Pixel 10a: Which Budget Phone Actually Makes More Sense?

content.rendered:
If you are shopping for a good phone without paying flagship prices, two devices are about to dominate the conversation in 2026: Apple’s iPhone 17e and Google’s Pixel 10a.

Both phones try to bring flagship‑level features to a much lower price. But they take very different approaches. Apple focuses on performance, battery life, and ecosystem features like MagSafe. Google leans heavily on AI features, camera flexibility, and a more affordable starting price.

So which one actually gives you more value? Let’s break it down piece by piece.

Table of Contents
  • Price and Storage: Which Phone Offers Better Value?
  • Design and Build Quality: Size, Materials, and Durability
  • Display Comparison: Brightness, Refresh Rate, and Clarity
  • Camera Comparison: iPhone 17e vs Pixel 10a Photography
  • Performance: Apple A19 vs Google Tensor G4
  • Battery Life and Charging: Which Phone Lasts Longer?
  • Connectivity: 5G, Wi-Fi, SIM Options, and Everyday Convenience
  • AI Features and Software: iOS 26 vs Android 16
  • iPhone 17e vs Pixel 10a: Quick Specs Comparison
  • Final Verdict: iPhone 17e or Pixel 10a – Which One Is Worth Buying?

Price and Storage: Which Phone Offers Better Value?

This is the first place most buyers look, and it quickly changes how the two phones compare on value. The Pixel starts cheaper, but storage is what makes the comparison more interesting.

Price is usually the first thing people check when picking a mid-range phone. At first glance, the Pixel 10a clearly looks like the better deal, starting at $499 compared to the iPhone 17e’s $599.

But storage shifts the comparison. The Pixel 10a begins with 128GB, while the iPhone 17e starts at 256GB.

Once you upgrade the Pixel to 256GB, its price rises to $599, which is exactly the same as the base iPhone 17e. Apple also offers a 512GB option for $799.

So while the Pixel has the lower entry price, the difference mostly disappears if you want the same amount of storage.

Design and Build Quality: Size, Materials, and Durability

Both phones aim to feel more manageable than today’s oversized flagships, but they get there in slightly different ways. The table covers the detailed specs, while the real takeaway comes down to size, materials, and a few practical design choices that affect daily use.

The first thing you will notice is the size. The iPhone 17e is a bit smaller and lighter, which can make it slightly easier to use with one hand and more comfortable in pockets.

In terms of durability, both phones are on similar ground. They use aluminum frames and carry the same IP68 water and dust resistance rating, so protection is not really a deciding factor here.

The back materials are different. The Pixel 10a uses a composite back, while the iPhone 17e uses ceramic. In everyday use, this mostly changes how the phone feels in the hand, and if you are using a case, the difference almost disappears.

Google also keeps its flush camera bar design. Instead of sticking out like many camera bumps, it sits flat with the back of the phone, which some people prefer for a cleaner look.

Display Comparison: Brightness, Refresh Rate, and Clarity

On paper, both displays look strong, but they prioritize different things. Apple focuses on sharpness and display clarity, while Google leans more toward brightness and smoother motion.

The main difference comes down to how the screens feel in everyday use.

The iPhone 17e has a sharper display, thanks to its higher pixel density. Text and fine details may look slightly crisper, which is something Apple tends to prioritize.

The Pixel 10a, however, focuses on smoothness and brightness. Its refresh rate can scale from 60Hz up to 120Hz, which makes scrolling, animations, and gaming feel noticeably smoother.

Brightness is another area where the Pixel stands out. With peak brightness reaching up to 3,000 nits, it should remain easier to see outdoors in strong sunlight.

Apple includes Ceramic Shield 2 protection and an anti-glare coating, which should help with durability and screen readability.

Camera Comparison: iPhone 17e vs Pixel 10a Photography

This is one of the biggest philosophical differences between the two phones. Apple keeps the camera system simple, while Google focuses on giving you more flexibility right out of the box.

The biggest difference is the number of cameras.

The iPhone 17e relies on a single 48MP main camera. Apple uses sensor cropping to offer a 2× zoom option, which works well for closer shots but still comes from the same main lens.

The Pixel 10a includes a second camera. Alongside the 48MP main sensor, it adds a 13MP ultra-wide camera. That extra lens makes it easier to capture landscapes, large buildings, and group photos without needing to step back.

Selfie cameras are fairly close. The Pixel uses a 13MP front camera, while the iPhone has a 12MP TrueDepth camera with a wider f/1.9 aperture, which can help capture more light in indoor or low-light selfies.

In terms of actual photo and video quality, both phones perform closer to flagship devices than their price suggests. Colors, detail, and overall image quality are strong on both sides. Each phone has its own style and quirks, but in practice, you are unlikely to go wrong with either option when it comes to the final results.

Google also leans heavily on computational photography. Features like Auto Best Take and Camera Coach use AI to help pick better shots or guide framing, giving the Pixel a few extra tools for people who like experimenting with photos.

Performance: Apple A19 vs Google Tensor G4

If speed matters to you, this section becomes especially important. The raw hardware gap here is one of the clearest differences in the entire comparison.

The biggest difference comes from the processor.

The iPhone 17e runs on Apple’s A19 chip, the same processor used in the standard iPhone 17. That gives it a clear advantage in raw speed and graphics performance.

Google uses the Tensor G4 in the Pixel 10a, which is the same chip used in the previous generation Pixel lineup. It is capable for everyday tasks, but it does not compete with Apple’s chip in pure performance.

That gap shows up clearly in benchmarks and heavier workloads. Tasks like gaming, exporting videos, or running demanding apps finish much faster on the iPhone.

For normal daily use, such as messaging, social media, navigation, and photography, both phones still feel smooth. But if you care about raw speed, gaming, or keeping the phone fast for many years, the iPhone 17e has a noticeable advantage here.

Battery Life and Charging: Which Phone Lasts Longer?

Battery and charging shape the daily experience more than people expect. This is also one area where official claims and real-world results do not always match perfectly.

The Pixel 10a looks stronger on paper. It includes a large 5,100 mAh battery and supports faster 30W wired charging.

The iPhone 17e does not list its battery capacity, but Apple claims up to 21 hours of video streaming. Apple’s efficiency with its chips and software often helps iPhones last longer than their battery size suggests.

In previous battery tests, iPhones have often outlasted Pixel phones under similar conditions, so real-world endurance may end up closer than the numbers suggest.

Charging features also differ. The iPhone 17e supports MagSafe with up to 15W wireless charging, which enables magnetic accessories like wallets, chargers, and car mounts.

The Pixel supports standard wireless charging at 10W, but it does not include Qi2 or magnetic accessory support.

Connectivity: 5G, Wi-Fi, SIM Options, and Everyday Convenience

These details are easy to overlook, but they start to matter once you use the phone every day. Wi-Fi support, SIM options, and small connectivity features can affect how convenient the phone feels in real life.

Most of the core connectivity features are the same. Both phones support Sub-6GHz 5G, LTE, and Bluetooth 6, so day-to-day connectivity will feel similar.

The Pixel 10a does have a small advantage with Wi-Fi 6E support, which allows access to faster 6GHz Wi-Fi networks if your router supports it.

SIM flexibility is another difference. The Pixel includes both eSIM support and a physical nano-SIM slot, while the iPhone 17e is fully eSIM-only.

For people who frequently swap SIM cards, travel often, or prefer using physical SIMs, the Pixel offers a bit more flexibility here.

AI Features and Software: iOS 26 vs Android 16

Software is where these phones begin to feel very different in real life. It is not just about iOS versus Android anymore, but also about how each company is approaching AI and system features.

The Pixel 10a runs Android 16 and centers much of its experience around Google’s Gemini AI system. Gemini powers a range of features directly across the phone.

Some of the most notable ones include Gemini Live for conversational interactions, Circle to Search for quick visual lookups, Pixel Studio for generating images, and Call Screening to filter unknown calls automatically.

The iPhone 17e runs iOS 26 with Apple Intelligence built into the system. Apple focuses more on integrating AI into everyday tools like writing assistance, notifications, and system personalization. Some generative tasks still rely on integrations such as ChatGPT.

Because of that, Google’s AI features currently feel broader and more deeply integrated across the system. Apple’s strength, on the other hand, is its clean interface and tight ecosystem integration with other Apple devices.

iPhone 17e vs Pixel 10a: Quick Specs Comparison

Before wrapping up, it helps to look at the major specs in one place. This gives you a cleaner view of where each phone is stronger before the final call.

Final Verdict: iPhone 17e or Pixel 10a – Which One Is Worth Buying?

The iPhone 17e and Pixel 10a take different approaches to the mid-range category.

The iPhone 17e stands out with a much faster processor, better long-term performance, higher base storage, and the MagSafe accessory ecosystem.

The Pixel 10a stands out with a lower starting price, a 120Hz display, an ultra-wide camera, and stronger built-in AI features.

Both phones deliver camera and video quality close to flagship devices, so image quality alone is unlikely to be a deciding factor.

If performance and ecosystem matter more, the iPhone 17e is the stronger choice. If price, display smoothness, and AI features matter more, the Pixel 10a offers better value.

For many buyers, the final decision will simply come down to iOS versus Android.

  • Google Pixel 11 Pro vs. iPhone 17 Pro

title.rendered: Apple’s First OLED MacBook May Be Called ‘MacBook Ultra’

content.rendered:
Apple may introduce an entirely new high-end laptop, the MacBook Ultra, later this year, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman. The device is rumored to feature an OLED display, touchscreen support, and a noticeably higher price point than existing MacBook models.

A New Tier Above the MacBook Pro

For months, reports suggested that Apple would bring OLED displays and touchscreen functionality to the next generation of MacBook Pro models powered by the upcoming M6 chip.

However, Gurman now suggests Apple could take a different approach. Instead of replacing the current MacBook Pro with M5 Pro and M5 Max models, the company may introduce a completely new flagship tier called the MacBook Ultra that sits above the MacBook Pro lineup.

This strategy would allow Apple to keep the MacBook Pro as a high-performance option while positioning the MacBook Ultra as the absolute top-end Mac laptop.

OLED Display and Touchscreen Support

One of the most significant rumored upgrades is an OLED display, which would mark the first time Apple uses OLED technology in a MacBook.

Apple has previously transitioned other products to OLED, including the iPhone X in 2017 and the iPad Pro in 2024. OLED panels provide deeper blacks, higher contrast ratios, and improved color accuracy compared with the current mini-LED displays used in MacBook Pro models.

The rumored MacBook Ultra may also include touchscreen functionality, something Apple has historically resisted on Mac laptops.

Higher Price Expected

If Apple follows its previous pattern, the shift to OLED could lead to a significant price increase.

When OLED debuted on the iPhone X and later on the iPad Pro, Apple increased pricing by roughly 20 percent. A similar bump could push the MacBook Ultra into a much higher price bracket than current MacBook Pro models.

Part of Apple’s Expanding Product Strategy

The MacBook Ultra would align with Apple’s broader strategy of expanding its product lineup across more price tiers.

At the lower end, Apple recently introduced the MacBook Neo, starting at $599, to compete with affordable Windows laptops and Chromebooks.

At the premium end, Apple is reportedly preparing several ultra-high-end devices, including:

  • A foldable iPhone Ultra priced around $2,000
  • New AirPods Ultra with computer vision cameras are designed to provide enhanced Visual Intelligence features

The MacBook Ultra could become the flagship Mac laptop within this growing Ultra tier of Apple products.

Possible Launch Timeline

Gurman expects the device to arrive toward the end of 2026, roughly the same timeframe as when Apple typically refreshes its MacBook Pro lineup.

Apple may still keep the MacBook Pro name for the device, but using the MacBook Ultra branding would clearly position it at the very top of the Mac lineup.

Would you buy a MacBook with an OLED display and touchscreen? Share your thoughts in the comments.

excerpt.rendered: Apple may launch a new MacBook Ultra with an OLED display and touchscreen, positioned above the MacBook Pro and expected to arrive in late 2026.

acceptedAnswer.text: Large updates may take several minutes. If the progress bar hasn’t moved for about one hour, the update may be stuck.

mainEntity.name: Will a force restart delete my data?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. A force restart only reboots the device and does not erase your files or settings.

mainEntity.name: Can full storage cause an iPhone to get stuck on the Apple logo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. If the device’s storage is completely full, iOS may fail to finish updating or starting. Freeing up space or restoring the device can fix the issue.

title.rendered: Does Aldi Take Apple Pay? (In-Store, Online & Self-Checkout)

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Aldi accepts Apple Pay in-store at both checkout lanes and self-checkouts, making it quick and easy to pay without reaching for your wallet.
  • How to pay in-store: Just open your Wallet app, choose your card, hold your iPhone or Apple Watch near the payment reader, and confirm with Face ID, Touch ID, or your passcode.
  • Instacart payments: You can use Apple Pay to pay for Aldi orders on the Instacart app or website. However, Instacart cards themselves won’t work with Apple Pay at Aldi’s physical registers.
  • Besides Apple Pay, Aldi also takes cash, debit cards, credit cards (Visa, MasterCard, Discover, AmEx), EBT, SNAP, and Link cards. However, they don’t accept checks or WIC benefits.
  • If Apple Pay fails at Aldi: Make sure your card is supported and has enough funds, try using another card, or reach out to your bank or Apple Support if it keeps happening.
  • Google Pay is also accepted at Aldi stores for another contactless payment option.

Aldi is the go-to store for many who order groceries online (using Instacart) or shop in-store at its various locations. The store’s popularity is due to its hard-to-beat retail prices on groceries and household items. On the flip side, the acceptance of Apple Pay as a payment method for online and in-store shopping has been rapid. Hence, I’ve been seeing questions like: Does Aldi accept Apple Pay?

If you’re reading this piece, it means you seek answers, too. In this guide, I’ll answer all your queries about Aldi’s payment mode and how to use Apple Pay at Aldi. Keep reading!

Does Aldi Accept Apple Pay?

Yes, Aldi accepts Apple Pay at its physical store locations in the United States. If you’re shopping in-store, you can tap your iPhone or Apple Watch at the contactless payment terminal to quickly and securely pay for your groceries without pulling out a card or cash.

Aldi began rolling out contactless payment support in 2018, and today nearly all registers, including self-checkout lanes, are equipped to handle Apple Pay along with other mobile wallets like Google Pay and Samsung Pay.

However, it’s important to note that Apple Pay is not accepted for online purchases through Aldi’s own systems (such as orders placed for delivery or pickup). If you’re ordering Aldi groceries through Instacart, Apple Pay is supported within the Instacart app or website. This applies only to online checkout through Instacart, not in-store payments.

Also, note that you can add your Instacart-issued cards to Apple Pay for use at Aldi’s physical registers. You need to use a debit or credit card linked to Apple Pay for in-store shopping.

How to Use Apple Pay at Aldi

You can use Apple Pay at Aldi stores to make payments, whether you choose self-checkout or traditional cashier-assisted checkout. It’s usually effortless, and I’ll guide you through the process below. Make sure you have already set up Apple Pay and follow the steps to use it at Aldi.

  1. Open the Wallet app on your iPhone or Apple Watch.
  2. Select the card you want to use to pay at the Aldi store. Note that Instacards are not currently accepted.
  3. Move your iPhone or Apple Watch to Aldi’s payment terminal or NFC card reader.
  4. You get a prompt to authenticate the payment with your Touch ID, Face ID, or passcode.
  5. Finally, keep your iPhone or Apple Watch on the NFC card reader or terminal at Aldi until the payment reads Done on your device.

Does Aldi Take Apple Pay for Instacart?

On the Instacart delivery app, you can check out your Aldi orders with Apple Pay. However, you cannot use your Instacard card as a payment option when paying with Apple Pay at Aldi stores. Here’s how to pay for your Aldi orders:

  1. Head to Instacart on your browser or its app.
  2. Select Aldi as your retailer and find the grocery items you want to shop.
  3. Proceed to the checkout page and select Apple Pay as your preferred payment method.
  4. Finally, check out and authenticate your payment with Face ID, Touch ID, or a passcode.

What Other Payment Methods Does Aldi Accept?

Apart from Apple Pay, Aldi accepts a range of payment methods in-store. Here’s a full breakdown:

One thing worth noting for EBT users: SNAP and EBT cards work at both cashier-assisted and self-checkout lanes at most Aldi locations. However, EBT cash benefits cannot be used for online Instacart orders, only in-store.

Aldi gift cards can be purchased in-store or online and used like a regular debit card at checkout. They do not work on Instacart.

Happy shopping…

Aldi accepts Apple Pay for in-store checkout. This method speeds up the checkout process and can be handy if you forget your card and need to pick up a few grocery items. To use Apple Pay, ensure you’ve linked your card to the Wallet app on your phone beforehand and use the steps I discuss to make your payments.

FAQs

Which Aldi stores accept Apple Pay outside of the USA?

Aldi stores accept Apple Pay everywhere except in regions where it isn’t fully supported. For instance, using Apple Pay at Aldi stores in China might be limited.

What should I do if my Apple Pay transaction at Aldi fails?

If your Apple Pay transaction fails at Apple, the following are the quick solutions I find helpful. You should confirm if your card is supported at Aldi, try a new card, and ensure the card has sufficient funds. If the issue persists, contact your card issuer or Apple support.

Can I use Apple Pay when ordering online at Aldi?

Aldi only accepts Apple Pay in-store. However, you can also use it to pay for online Aldi orders via Instacart.

Does Aldi take Apple Pay in the UK?

Yes, Aldi stores in the UK accept Apple Pay. Contactless payments are widely supported across Aldi’s UK locations, and Apple Pay works at all checkout terminals there.

Does Aldi take Apple Pay in Australia?

Yes, Aldi Australia accepts Apple Pay. Contactless payment is standard across their Australian stores.

Does Aldi accept Samsung Pay?

Yes, Aldi accepts Samsung Pay alongside Apple Pay and Google Pay at all US store locations.

Read more on Apple Pay:

  • Does Target take Apple Pay?
  • Does Walmart accept Apple Pay?
  • Does Dunkin take Apple Pay?
  • Does CVS take Apple Pay?
  • What stores take Apple Pay?

title.rendered: How to Share Screen on WhatsApp (iPhone, Android, and Desktop)

content.rendered:
Screen sharing on WhatsApp is useful when you want to show someone what’s happening on your device instead of explaining it. Whether you’re helping a family member troubleshoot an issue, showing a document, or guiding a friend through an app, WhatsApp’s screen-sharing feature lets you share your display in real time.

This guide explains how to share your screen on iOS, Android, and desktop, along with quick fixes if the option isn’t available.

Table of Contents
  • Things to Know Before Sharing Your Screen on WhatsApp
  • How to Share Your Screen on WhatsApp for iPhone and Android
    • On iPhone
    • On Android
  • Share Your Screen on WhatsApp Desktop (Mac and Windows)
    • On Mac
    • On Windows
  • Why You Might Not See the Screen Share Option
  • How to Fix WhatsApp Screen Sharing Not Working
  • Final Thoughts

Things to Know Before Sharing Your Screen on WhatsApp

Before you start, keep these important points in mind:

  • Screen sharing works only during an active WhatsApp video call. It is not available during audio calls.
  • You can use screen sharing on iOS, Android, and the WhatsApp Desktop app for Mac and Windows.
  • WhatsApp confirms that screen sharing is protected by end-to-end encryption, meaning only people in the call can see your screen.
  • Everything visible on your screen will be shared, including notifications, messages, and sensitive information. It’s best to enable Do Not Disturb before starting.

How to Share Your Screen on WhatsApp for iPhone and Android

On iPhone

Mobile devices are one of the most common ways to share your screen on WhatsApp. Follow these steps on your iPhone or iPad:

  1. Open WhatsApp and start a video call.
  2. Tap the three-dot icon in the call controls.
  3. Select Share screen.
  4. Select Start Broadcast to begin sharing.

To stop sharing, tap Stop Broadcast on the call screen.

On Android

Screen sharing on Android is simple and works similarly to iOS. Here’s how to do it:

  1. Start or join a video call in WhatsApp.
  2. Tap the three-dot icon at the bottom of the call screen.
  3. Select Share screen.
  4. A warning pop-up box about screen sharing will appear.
  5. Allow the required permissions and tap Start now.

When you’re finished, tap Stop Sharing on the call screen.

Share Your Screen on WhatsApp Desktop (Mac and Windows)

WhatsApp Web does not currently support screen sharing or voice/video calls. However, you can share your screen using the WhatsApp Desktop app on Mac or Windows.

On Mac

  1. Open the WhatsApp app on your Mac and start a video call.
  2. Click the Screen Sharing icon.
  3. A permission pop-up will appear; click Allow to enable screen and audio sharing.
  4. Choose the screen or window you want to share.
  5. Click Share.

To stop sharing:

  • Click Stop Sharing inside WhatsApp, or
  • Click the purple screen-sharing icon in the macOS menu bar and select Stop Sharing.

On Windows

  1. Open WhatsApp Desktop on your Windows PC.
  2. Start a video call.
  3. Click the Screen Sharing icon.
  4. Choose a screen, window, or tab to share.
  5. Click Share.
  6. To stop sharing, click Stop sharing in WhatsApp.

Related: How to Share Screen on Instagram Video Calls

Why You Might Not See the Screen Share Option

If the screen-sharing button is missing, it may be due to one of the following reasons:

  • You started an audio call instead of a video call.
  • Your WhatsApp app is outdated.
  • Required system permissions are disabled on your device.
  • On desktop, camera access may be blocked, preventing the feature from appearing.

How to Fix WhatsApp Screen Sharing Not Working

If screen sharing isn’t working on WhatsApp, try these troubleshooting steps:

  • Update WhatsApp from the App Store, Google Play Store, or Microsoft Store.
  • Check permissions for camera, microphone, and screen recording.
  • Disable aggressive battery optimization or background restrictions.
  • Restart or reinstall the WhatsApp app.
  • Switch to a stable internet connection.

Related: 11 Ways to Fix WhatsApp Calls Not Working on iPhone and Android

Final Thoughts

WhatsApp screen sharing makes it easy to explain something visually without leaving the app. It’s simple, secure, and convenient for quick help, demonstrations, or presentations.

If you need advanced features such as remote control, annotations, or high-quality audio sharing, dedicated tools like Zoom or Microsoft Teams may work better. However, for everyday use, WhatsApp’s built-in screen sharing works well.

FAQs

Can you share your screen without a video call on WhatsApp?

No. Screen sharing only works during an active WhatsApp video call.

Does WhatsApp screen sharing work on Mac?

Yes. Screen sharing works in the WhatsApp Desktop app for Mac, although some features may be limited compared to Windows.

Can others record your shared screen?

WhatsApp does not record screen-sharing sessions. However, participants in the call could use their own devices to record the screen.

Does WhatsApp screen sharing include system audio?

System audio sharing depends on your device and operating system, so it may not always work the same way across platforms.

Also read:

  • How to Hide WhatsApp Message Preview on iPhone

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Screen sharing only works during an active WhatsApp video call.

mainEntity.name: Does WhatsApp screen sharing work on Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Screen sharing works in the WhatsApp Desktop app for Mac, although some features may be limited compared to Windows.

mainEntity.name: Can others record your shared screen?

acceptedAnswer.text: WhatsApp does not record screen-sharing sessions. However, participants in the call could use their own devices to record the screen.

mainEntity.name: Does WhatsApp screen sharing include system audio?

acceptedAnswer.text: System audio sharing depends on your device and operating system, so it may not always work the same way across platforms.

title.rendered: First MacBook Neo Benchmarks Reveal Power of Apple’s A18 Pro Chip

content.rendered:
The first benchmark results for Apple’s newly announced MacBook Neo are now online, offering an early look at how the A18 Pro performs inside a Mac.

The results show that Apple’s iPhone chip delivers performance that is surprisingly competitive with entry-level Mac processors. The MacBook Neo scored 3,461 in single-core tests and 8,668 in multi-core tests, numbers that closely match those of the iPhone 16 Pro.

The reason is simple. Both devices run the same A18 Pro chip, though the MacBook Neo ships with a slightly reduced GPU configuration.

GPU Difference Explains Metal Score Gap

Graphics performance is where the first difference appears. The MacBook Neo recorded a Metal score of 31,286, slightly lower than the iPhone 16 Pro’s 32,575. This gap exists because the MacBook Neo includes one fewer GPU core.

Aside from graphics, the CPU results are almost identical between the two devices.

How the MacBook Neo Stacks Up Against Other Apple Devices

Looking beyond the iPhone comparison, the MacBook Neo delivers performance that lands in an interesting spot within Apple’s lineup.

The numbers reveal a shift. While the Neo cannot match the multi-core power of newer M-series chips, its single-core performance is far ahead of the original M1 MacBook Air.

Related: MacBook Neo vs MacBook Air: Full Comparison (Specs, Price, Features)

Why Strong Single-Core Performance Matters?

Single-core speed still plays a major role in many everyday computing tasks.

Activities such as browsing websites, opening apps, writing documents, and watching videos often depend more on single-thread performance than raw multi-core throughput. In these areas, the A18 Pro performs extremely well.

That makes the MacBook Neo well-suited for students, casual users, and people who mainly use a laptop for productivity and media.

Apple is Targeting a Different Segment

Apple is not positioning the MacBook Neo against its own Mac lineup. Instead, the company is aiming directly at budget laptops powered by Windows or ChromeOS.

Apple claims the A18 Pro is:

  • up to 50% faster in everyday tasks than the best-selling PC with an Intel Core Ultra 5 processor
  • up to three times faster for on-device AI workloads
  • up to twice as fast for photo editing

This positioning explains the Neo’s aggressive starting price.

Related: A18 Pro vs M1: How Apple’s iPhone Chip Compares to the First Mac Silicon

Price and Availability

The MacBook Neo starts at $599, making it the most affordable Mac Apple currently sells.

Preorders are already open, and the laptop will begin shipping on March 11.

More benchmark entries will likely appear over the coming days, which should give a clearer picture of real-world performance. Early results already confirm one thing. Apple’s iPhone chips are now powerful enough to comfortably power entry-level Macs.

Would you buy the MacBook Neo based on these benchmarks? Tell us in the comments below.

To get the most out of your MacBook Neo, the right accessories are essential. They can boost productivity, expand connectivity, and keep your mac protected.

title.rendered: A18 Pro vs M1: How Apple’s iPhone Chip Compares to the First Mac Silicon

content.rendered:
Apple transitioned away from Intel to Apple Silicon in 2020 with the introduction of the M1 chip. Devices powered by the M1 chip, such as the MacBook Air and Mac mini, set a new benchmark for performance and efficiency.

Fast forward four years, Apple introduced the A18 Pro chip in the iPhone 16 Pro, which has now appeared in the company’s new entry-level laptop, the MacBook Neo.

This development raises an interesting question. How does the A18 Pro compare with the M1 chip that started Apple’s Mac silicon journey? Let’s take a closer look at how these two Apple chips compare.

Table of Contents
  • Apple A18 Pro vs M1: Quick Comparison
  • Apple A18 Pro vs M1: CPU Performance
    • Single-Core Performance
    • Multi-Core Performance
  • Apple A18 Pro vs M1: GPU Performance
  • A18 Pro vs M1: AI and Neural Engine
  • A18 Pro vs M1: Efficiency and Power Consumption
  • A18 Pro vs M1: Which Chip Is Better?
  • Why is Apple Using the A18 Pro in the MacBook Neo?
  • Final Verdict

Apple A18 Pro vs M1: Quick Comparison

Apple A18 Pro vs M1: CPU Performance

Starting with the CPU, the Apple M1 chip is built on TSMC’s 5nm process, while the newer A18 Pro uses a more advanced 3nm manufacturing node. The smaller process helps the A18 Pro achieve higher efficiency and improved performance.

Single-Core Performance

The A18 Pro delivers noticeably stronger single-core performance in my tests.

It scored 1840 in Geekbench 6’s single-core test, compared to the M1’s 1463. This means the newer chip performs better in tasks that rely on a single CPU core.

Single-core performance affects everyday tasks such as:

  • launching apps
  • browsing the web
  • scrolling through interfaces
  • opening documents

This is also one reason Apple can use the A18 Pro in the MacBook Neo, where fast everyday responsiveness matters more than sustained heavy workloads.

Multi-Core Performance

Multi-core results tell a slightly different story. The M1 scored 4616, while the A18 Pro scored 4362 in Geekbench 6 multi-core tests.

This advantage comes from the M1’s 8-core CPU design, which includes four performance cores and four efficiency cores. Macs also operate within higher power limits, allowing them to maintain performance under sustained workloads.

For tasks such as video rendering, code compilation, and large multitasking workloads, the M1 still has a slight advantage.

Apple A18 Pro vs M1: GPU Performance

Moving to GPU performance, Apple has significantly improved graphics capabilities in its recent A-series chips. The 6-core GPU on the A18 Pro chip introduces architectural improvements and higher efficiency compared to earlier Apple silicon.

In my Geekbench GPU tests, the MacBook Air (M1, 2020) powered by the Apple M1 chip scored 21,417 in the Metal benchmark. Meanwhile, the iPhone 16 Pro with the A18 Pro achieved a Metal score of 18,352.

While the M1 still delivers stronger raw GPU performance in this test, the difference is surprisingly small, given that the A18 Pro is designed for a smartphone. Apple’s improvements in GPU architecture and efficiency allow the chip to deliver competitive graphics performance despite operating within a much smaller power envelope.

In real-world usage, both chips can comfortably handle tasks such as photo editing, casual gaming, UI rendering, and graphics-heavy apps.

This level of graphics performance also explains why Apple can power devices like the MacBook Neo with the A18 Pro while still delivering smooth everyday graphics performance.

A18 Pro vs M1: AI and Neural Engine

Both chips feature Apple’s 16-core Neural Engine, but the newer A18 Pro chip brings noticeable improvements in machine learning capabilities and efficiency. Apple continues to refine its AI hardware each generation to support more advanced on-device intelligence.

The Neural Engine on the A18 Pro delivers up to 35 trillion operations per second (TOPS), enabling faster processing for tasks such as image recognition, natural language processing, and AI-powered photo editing. In comparison, the Apple M1 chip offers around 11 TOPS of AI compute, which was impressive at the time of its launch but now falls behind newer Apple silicon.

The stronger AI engine allows devices like the iPhone 16 Pro to run advanced machine learning workloads directly on the device. These include features such as real-time image processing, voice recognition, and on-device AI tasks.

With Apple increasingly focusing on AI-powered features across its platforms, the improved Neural Engine in the A18 Pro also helps devices like the MacBook Neo handle modern AI workloads more efficiently while maintaining excellent power efficiency.

A18 Pro vs M1: Efficiency and Power Consumption

The A18 Pro chip is built on TSMC’s 3nm process, which allows it to deliver higher performance while consuming less power. In comparison, the Apple M1 chip is manufactured using TSMC’s 5nm process. While the M1 was highly efficient when it launched in 2020, the smaller 3nm node gives the A18 Pro a clear performance advantage per watt.

Another key factor is the target device class. The A18 Pro is designed primarily for smartphones like the iPhone 16 Pro, where power efficiency is critical to maintain long battery life in a compact form factor. The M1, on the other hand, powers larger devices such as the MacBook Air (M1, 2020), which can operate within higher power limits for sustained workloads.

Despite these differences, both chips are extremely efficient compared to traditional laptop processors. The improved efficiency of the A18 Pro is also what allows Apple to power devices like the MacBook Neo with a smartphone-class processor while still delivering strong everyday performance and excellent battery life.

A18 Pro vs M1: Which Chip Is Better?

Neither chip outshines the other, as both are impressive and excel in different areas.

A18 Pro advantages

  • Faster single-core performance
  • Competitive GPU performance in some workloads
  • Newer architecture
  • Better power efficiency

M1 advantages

  • Better sustained performance
  • More CPU cores
  • Designed specifically for Mac workloads
  • Higher multi-core performance

Why is Apple Using the A18 Pro in the MacBook Neo?

Apple’s decision to power the MacBook Neo with the A18 Pro chip highlights how far its mobile silicon has evolved in recent years. Even though the A18 Pro was originally designed for smartphones like the iPhone 16 Pro, its performance is now strong enough to compete with early Apple Silicon Mac chips, such as the Apple M1. As our benchmarks show, the A18 Pro delivers competitive CPU and GPU performance while maintaining excellent efficiency.

At the same time, the A18 Pro’s 3nm architecture enables outstanding power efficiency. This allows the MacBook Neo to deliver long battery life while maintaining a thin and fanless design.

Ultimately, using the A18 Pro helps Apple position the MacBook Neo as a more affordable entry-level Mac while still delivering modern performance and efficiency. For most everyday users, the chip provides more than enough power to run macOS smoothly.

Final Verdict

The A18 Pro and M1 represent two different phases of Apple Silicon evolution. The M1 marked the beginning of the Mac transition away from Intel and delivered incredible performance for laptops in 2020. But Apple’s mobile chips have improved rapidly since then.

Today, the A18 Pro matches or even exceeds the M1 in several areas, including single-core performance and AI processing. With Apple now using the chip in devices like the MacBook Neo, it’s clear that the line between iPhone chips and Mac processors is becoming thinner every year.

What are your thoughts on Apple using the A18 Pro in MacBook Neo? Join the discussion in the comments.

title.rendered: MacBook Neo vs MacBook Air: Full Comparison (Specs, Price, Features)

content.rendered:
Apple’s Mac lineup now includes a wider range of laptops than ever before. At the entry level is the new MacBook Neo, a budget-friendly option to make the Mac experience more accessible. Above it sits the MacBook Air, which is the mainstream ultraportable Mac for the masses.

The MacBook Neo focuses on the basic everyday tasks like web browsing, streaming videos, writing documents, and light productivity work. However, the MacBook Air is built for users who need more performance, better hardware features, and stronger multitasking capabilities. As the Neo model is priced way lower than the Air, there are many tradeoffs.

In this guide, I’ll share a detailed comparison of MacBook Neo vs. MacBook Air, including their specs, design, performance, battery life, and price, so you can decide which is better for everyday use.

Table of Contents
  • MacBook Neo vs MacBook Air: Quick Comparison
  • Design and Build Quality
  • Performance: A-Series vs M-Series Chips
  • Display Comparison
  • RAM and Storage Options
  • Ports and Connectivity
  • Keyboard, Touch ID, Camera, Mic, and Speaker Specs
  • Battery Life Compared
  • MacBook Neo vs. MacBook Air: Price and Value
    • Final Verdict: Which MacBook Should You Buy?

MacBook Neo vs MacBook Air: Quick Comparison

The table makes the positioning clear: MacBook Neo is the budget Mac, while MacBook Air is the more powerful everyday laptop. Now let’s break it down further!

Design and Build Quality

In terms of overall look, both laptops follow Apple’s familiar minimalist design. They use aluminum bodies, slim profiles, and large trackpads.

The MacBook Neo looks similar to the Air but includes a few cost-saving changes. It has thicker display bezels and a slightly thicker body, although the overall size and weight are close to the Air. The laptop weighs about 2.7 pounds, which is nearly identical to the MacBook Air.

Apple also introduced more playful colors for the Neo, including Silver, Blush, Citrus, and Indigo, which gives it a slightly more casual and student-friendly look. These colors extend to its Magic keyboard as opposed to the black backlit keyboard on the Air.

The MacBook Air, by contrast, is built as a premium ultraportable device. It features thinner edges, a more refined chassis, and a slightly larger display in a similarly compact body. Apple positions it as the laptop most people should buy if they want a balance of portability and performance.

Overall, the build quality of both machines is excellent, but the MacBook Air feels more premium and refined, while the Neo focuses on affordability.

Performance: A-Series vs M-Series Chips

The biggest technical difference between the two laptops is the processor.

The MacBook Neo uses Apple’s A18 Pro chip, which originally debuted in the iPhone lineup. This chip includes:

  • 6-core CPU with 2 performance cores and 4 efficiency cores
  • 5-core GPU
  • 16-core Neural Engine
  • 60GB/s memory bandwidth

While that may sound impressive, the A-series chip is designed primarily for iPhones, not full computers. As a result, its performance is suitable for everyday tasks but not heavy workloads. Some of the tasks that the Neo can handle well include web surfing, streaming videos, writing documents, online classes, and basic photo editing.

On the other hand, the MacBook Air runs Apple’s M-series chips such as the M5. These chips are designed specifically for Macs and deliver much higher performance.

For example, the M5 chip can include:

  • 10-core CPU with 4 super cores and 6 efficiency cores
  • 8-core or higher GPU with integrated Neural Accelerators
  • 16-core Neural Engine
  • 153GB/s memory bandwidth

Therefore, it’s 20% faster for single-core tasks and 80% faster for multi-core tasks than A18 Pro chips. This makes the MacBook Air significantly better for tasks like video editing, programming, graphic design, large spreadsheets, and heavy multitasking.

So, in terms of performance comparison, the MacBook Neo is good for light computing, while the MacBook Air is built for demanding workloads.

Display Comparison

Both laptops use Apple’s Liquid Retina display technology, but there are still several differences.

The MacBook Neo features a 13-inch Liquid Retina display with a resolution of 2408 × 1506 pixels and brightness of about 500 nits. However, it lacks several advanced display technologies, including True Tone support and P3 wide color gamut.

Instead, it uses a more basic sRGB color range, which means colors are slightly less vibrant than on higher-end Macs. Also, the display bezels are slightly thicker for cost-cutting.

The MacBook Air offers a more advanced display. It’s available in larger 13.6-inch and 15-inch screen, 2560 by 1664 pixel resolution, wider P3 color support, and additional technologies that improve color accuracy and viewing comfort.

For everyday use, like watching videos or browsing the web, both screens look great. But for photo editing, design work, or color-sensitive tasks, the MacBook Air clearly has the better display.

RAM and Storage Options

Memory and storage options are another major difference between the two laptops.

The MacBook Neo is limited to 8GB of unified memory, and there is no option to upgrade it. Storage starts at 256GB and can be upgraded to 512GB. For light users, this configuration is usually enough. But for people who run many apps at once or work with large files, the limitation can become noticeable.

But the MacBook Air is far more flexible. It starts with 16GB of RAM and offers upgrade options such as 24GB or 32GB RAM, and has storage options up to 4TB. This means the MacBook Air can handle much heavier workloads and remain useful for many years.

Ports and Connectivity

Connectivity is another area where the MacBook Air offers more advanced features.

The MacBook Neo includes two USB-C ports and a 3.5mm headphone jack. However, these USB-C ports are limited in speed. One supports USB 3 (10 Gb/s) and the other only USB 2 speeds (480 Mb/s). It also supports only one external 4K display at 60Hz.

On the other hand, the MacBook Air offers a much stronger port setup:

  • Two Thunderbolt 4 ports (40 Gb/s speeds)
  • MagSafe 3 charging port
  • 3.5mm headphone jack

It can also support multiple external displays, including up to two 6K displays, depending on the configuration. So, in everyday use, the MacBook Air works much better with docks, external monitors, and professional accessories.

Keyboard, Touch ID, Camera, Mic, and Speaker Specs

The MacBook Neo includes Apple’s Magic Keyboard and a large trackpad, but there are a few compromises to keep the price low.

For example:

  • The keyboard does not include backlighting.
  • The base model only has a Lock key. For Touch ID, you need the 512GB model.
  • It uses a standard mechanical multi-touch trackpad instead of the Force Touch trackpad found in other Macs.

The Neo still includes useful hardware such as a 1080p FaceTime HD camera, dual microphones with voice isolation and directional beamforming, and dual stereo speakers with Spatial Audio and Dolby Atmos support. So, you can enjoy music and video streaming.

In contrast, the MacBook Air offers a more premium input and audio experience. It includes:

  • Backlit Magic Keyboard
  • Touch ID on all models
  • Force Touch trackpad
  • 12MP Center Stage camera with Desk View support
  • LED webcam indicator light and Ambient light sensor
  • Improved four speakers and a three-mic array

These upgrades make the MacBook Air better for video calls, music, movies, and long typing sessions.

Battery Life Compared

Battery life takes a major place in the MacBook Neo vs. MacBook Air comparison. Thanks to Apple’s efficient silicon chips, both laptops can survive day-to-day usage.

The MacBook Neo includes a 36.5-watt-hour lithium-ion battery and can last up to:

  • 11 hours of web browsing
  • 16 hours of video playback

The MacBook Air has a larger 53.8-watt-hour lithium-polymer battery and can reach:

  • 15 hours of web browsing
  • 18 hours of video playback

Both laptops easily last a full day for typical use, but the MacBook Air usually lasts slightly longer.

Another difference is charging. The Neo charges through 20W USB-C only, while the Air includes MagSafe charging, which frees up ports and disconnects safely if the cable is pulled. It supports a 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with a 60W Max.

MacBook Neo vs. MacBook Air: Price and Value

The biggest difference between the two laptops is price.

The MacBook Neo starts at $599, making it Apple’s cheapest MacBook ever, whereas the MacBook Air starts at $1,099, which is about $500 more expensive.

That price difference reflects the hardware improvements in the Air, including:

  • Faster M-series processor
  • Better display
  • More RAM and storage options
  • Thunderbolt connectivity
  • MagSafe charging
  • Longer battery life

So the choice really comes down to budget vs performance.

If you only need a simple laptop for everyday computing, the MacBook Neo offers excellent value. But if you want a more powerful laptop that will last longer and handle demanding tasks, the MacBook Air is worth the extra cost.

Final Verdict: Which MacBook Should You Buy?

The MacBook Neo and MacBook Air are designed for very different types of users.

The MacBook Neo is best for students, casual users, families buying multiple laptops, first-time Mac buyers, and basic everyday computing. It delivers the core macOS experience at the lowest price Apple has ever offered. The MacBook Air is better for professionals, creators and developers, heavy multitaskers, and users who want a long-term laptop.

If your needs are simple and budget matters most, the MacBook Neo is a great entry point into the Mac ecosystem. But if you want stronger performance, better features, and a laptop that can handle more demanding tasks over time, the MacBook Air remains the better overall MacBook for most people.

What’s your thoughts? Let us know in the comments below!

title.rendered: 8 Must-Have Accessories for Your New iPhone 17e

content.rendered:
That first week with a new iPhone is always the same. You handle it like it is made of glass, avoid pockets with keys, and plug it in before the battery dips too low.

Accessories are how you keep that “new phone care” going later without thinking about it.

A solid case and screen protector take the hit from daily scuffs. And now that the iPhone 17e supports MagSafe, you can set up cleaner charging at your desk or carry a magnetic power bank when you are out. There are also MagSafe add-ons that make quick errands simpler.

Here are eight essential accessories for your new iPhone 17e that protect and enhance it without adding bulk.

Table of Contents
  • 1. Apple iPhone 17e Silicone Case
  • 2. Spigen Ultra Hybrid (MagFit) Case
  • 3. IMBZBK Screen Protector
  • 4. Apple FineWoven MagSafe Wallet
  • 5. Anker 3-in-1 Cube Charging Station
  • 6. Anker Nano MagSafe Power Bank
  • 7. LISEN Magnetic Car Mount
  • 8. AirPods Pro 3
  • The Quick Setup that Covers Everything

1. Apple iPhone 17e Silicone Case

If you want a slim case that protects the phone without making it bulky, Apple’s official silicone case is usually the easiest pick. It’s a thin silicone shell with a soft-touch exterior (Apple says it’s made from 45% recycled silicone), and the inside has a microfiber lining so the back of the phone rests against fabric instead of plastic.

There is a small raised lip around the screen and camera module, so they are not the first things to touch a table. The case also has Apple’s built-in magnet ring, which keeps MagSafe wallets and battery packs properly aligned and allows charging on MagSafe or Qi2 pads without removing the case. It also works with crossbody straps if you prefer carrying your phone hands-free. Color options include Black, Anchor Blue, Bright Guava, Light Moss, Soft Pink, and Vanilla.

At $49, it is more expensive than many third-party cases, but it remains a dependable choice if you want a slim case that fits well, protects the phone, and works cleanly with MagSafe accessories.

Check out on Apple Store

2. Spigen Ultra Hybrid (MagFit) Case

If you like seeing the actual color and design of your iPhone 17e, a clear case usually makes more sense than covering it up. Spigen’s Ultra Hybrid (MagFit) does exactly that with a transparent polycarbonate back and flexible TPU edges that wrap around the frame.

That combination is the main reason people pick this case. The rigid back keeps the case clear and scratch-resistant, while the softer TPU bumper helps absorb impacts if the phone falls. Spigen also adds its Air Cushion pockets in the corners, which are designed to take most of the shock during drops.

There is a raised edge around the screen and camera so they do not rest directly on a table. The case also includes a magnet ring for MagSafe accessories and wireless charging. Spigen’s magnets are known to be quite strong, which helps wallets, stands, and battery packs stay firmly attached.

It is priced at $44.99 in the US and comes in several clear variants like Clear White, Clear Graphite, Clear Gold, Clear Deep Blue, and Clear Orange. If you want protection but still want the phone’s design to remain visible, this is one of the more practical clear cases to consider.

Check out on Amazon

3. IMBZBK Screen Protector

A screen protector is one of the easiest ways to avoid scratches on the iPhone 17e’s display, and IMBZBK’s tempered glass pack is a practical option because it usually comes with three protectors in the box. It typically sells for around $12–$15 on Amazon, which means you have spares if the first one cracks or the installation goes wrong.

The kit includes an alignment frame, cleaning wipes, and dust stickers. The frame sits on the phone and helps place the glass in the correct position, which makes installation much easier compared to applying a protector by hand.

The glass is thin and transparent, with an oleophobic coating to reduce fingerprints and smudges. It is also cut to be case-friendly, so most cases will not lift the edges. Some versions of the pack also include camera lens protectors, and there are variants such as clear, matte anti-glare, and privacy glass, depending on what you prefer.

Check out on Amazon

4. Apple FineWoven MagSafe Wallet

If you prefer carrying just a few cards instead of a full wallet, Apple’s FineWoven MagSafe Wallet attaches magnetically to the back of the iPhone 17e or a MagSafe case and holds up to three cards, such as a credit card, ID, or transit card.

It’s made from Apple’s FineWoven microtwill material using 100% recycled content and has a soft, suede-like texture. The wallet also includes RFID shielding to help protect cards from unwanted scanning.

One useful feature is Find My support. Once paired with your iPhone, it can show the wallet’s last known location in the Find My app if it gets separated from the phone.

It costs $59 in the US and comes in colors like Black, Navy, Fox Orange, Moss, and Pacific Blue. If you already use MagSafe accessories, it’s a clean way to carry a couple of cards without bringing a separate wallet.

Check out on Amazon

5. Anker 3-in-1 Cube Charging Station

If you charge multiple Apple devices every day, the Anker 3-in-1 Cube keeps everything in one place. It’s a compact charging station that powers an iPhone 17e, Apple Watch, and AirPods at the same time.

The cube unfolds to reveal a magnetic Qi2 charging pad for the iPhone, a pop-up Apple Watch charger, and a flat spot for AirPods with wireless charging. The iPhone pad delivers up to 15W wireless charging and snaps into alignment magnetically.

When folded, the whole charger turns into a small cube measuring about 3.3 inches on each side, which makes it easy to pack for travel or keep on a desk without taking up much space. The box also includes a 40W USB-C charger and cable.

It sells for $129.99 in the US. If you use an iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods together, this kind of charger simplifies the setup by replacing three separate charging cables with one compact dock.

Check out on Amazon

6. Anker Nano MagSafe Power Bank

If you want a backup battery without carrying cables, Anker’s Nano magnetic power bank snaps onto the back of the iPhone 17e and starts charging wirelessly.

It has a 5,000mAh capacity, which is usually enough to give the phone roughly one extra charge depending on usage. It supports up to 15W wireless charging and also includes a USB-C port for pass-through charging, so you can recharge the power bank while it is attached to the phone.

The main advantage is its size. At about half an inch thick, it stays fairly pocket-friendly compared to larger magnetic batteries. Some versions also include a small kickstand for propping the phone up while watching videos.

It typically sells for around $40–$50 in the US and comes in colors like Black, White, and Blue.

Check out Best Buy

7. LISEN Magnetic Car Mount

If you use your iPhone 17e for navigation in the car, a MagSafe-style mount is much easier than the old clamp-style holders. The LISEN magnetic car mount lets you snap your phone onto it and remove it in a second.

It uses strong magnets to hold the phone in place, and the base attaches to the dashboard using a 3M adhesive pad. Once installed, the arm and mount can be adjusted to position the phone at a comfortable viewing angle while driving.

The mount works with the iPhone 17e and other MagSafe-compatible cases. It does not include wireless charging, but the magnetic attachment keeps the phone stable even on rough roads.

Depending on the model, it usually sells for around $17–$30 in the US. If you regularly use Apple Maps, Google Maps, or Waze while driving, a magnetic mount like this makes the iPhone much easier and safer to use in the car.

Check out on Amazon

8. AirPods Pro 3

If you are using an iPhone 17e, AirPods Pro 3 work seamlessly with it. Pairing is instant through Apple’s automatic setup, and features like Spatial Audio, head tracking, and device switching work smoothly across Apple devices.

They use Apple’s H3 chip for Active Noise Cancellation, Adaptive Audio, and Transparency mode. The charging case also includes a U2 chip, which enables Precision Finding in the Find My app when used with newer iPhones like the 17e.

The earbuds include custom drivers for clear sound, touch controls with swipe gestures for volume, and silicone tips in multiple sizes for a secure fit. Both the earbuds and the case are rated IP54 for dust, sweat, and water resistance.

Battery life is rated at up to 6 hours with noise cancellation on, and up to 30 hours with the charging case. The case supports USB-C and wireless charging. AirPods Pro 3 are priced at $249 in the US.

Check out on Amazon

The Quick Setup that Covers Everything

If you want the simple, balanced kit:

  • Choose a case: Apple Silicone for the cleanest fit, or Spigen Ultra Hybrid to show off the phone
  • Add protection: IMBZBK screen protector
  • Use MagSafe well: FineWoven wallet for daily carry, 3-in-1 Cube for home charging, Nano power bank for travel

This is the combination that keeps the iPhone 17e protected, makes charging easier, and adds just enough utility to feel like an upgrade without turning your phone into a project.

  • Buy iPhone 17e Now or Wait for iPhone 18
  • iPhone 17e vs iPhone 17

title.rendered: How to Turn Off Location on Snapchat (Step-by-Step Guide)

content.rendered:
Snapchat’s Snap Map is a fun way to discover what’s happening around you, letting you explore snaps and stories from friends and nearby users. However, it also shows your location to friends on the map when location sharing is enabled, which might raise privacy concerns for some users.

To help protect users’ privacy, Snapchat lets you share your location with specific friends, hide it from certain people, turn it off for everyone using Ghost Mode, or completely disable location access in your phone’s settings.

Keep reading to learn how Snapchat location sharing works and how to turn off location on Snapchat.

Table of Contents
  • What Is Snapchat Location Sharing and How Does It Work?
  • How to Turn Off Location on Snapchat
    • Method 1: Turn On Ghost Mode on Snapchat
    • Method 2: Hide Your Snapchat Location From Specific Friends
    • Method 3: Disable Snapchat Location Access From Phone Settings
    • On iPhone:
    • On Android:
  • Does Snapchat Track Your Location When the App Is Closed?
  • What Happens When You Turn Off Location on Snapchat?
    • Summing Up

What Is Snapchat Location Sharing and How Does It Work?

Location sharing is a Snap Map feature that updates your approximate location on the map every time you open the Snapchat app. It helps users discover nearby snaps, view local stories, and know where friends are when they are active on the app.

All your friends on the platform can view your location on the live map through your Bitmoji. The visibility of your location depends on your privacy settings, which let you share it with all friends, selected friends, or no one using Ghost Mode.

If you don’t use Snapchat for a while, your location automatically disappears from Snap Map. Additionally, you can completely disable location access at any time in your phone’s settings for added privacy.

How to Turn Off Location on Snapchat

As previously mentioned, Snapchat lets you turn off your location on the Snap Map entirely or for selected friends, while still keeping location access enabled for other purposes.

Method 1: Turn On Ghost Mode on Snapchat

Ghost Mode on Snapchat lets you turn off your location on the Snap Map while still allowing you to view friends’ locations when they have location sharing enabled.

  1. Open the Snapchat app and tap the Snap Map (Location Pin) icon in the bottom-left corner.
  2. Tap the Settings icon.
  3. Toggle on Ghost Mode.
  4. Select the Until Turned Off option in the pop-up menu that appears.

Method 2: Hide Your Snapchat Location From Specific Friends

If you don’t want to disappear completely but prefer to hide your location from certain friends, Snapchat lets you customize who can see your location.

  1. Tap the Settings icon on the Snap Map tab.
  2. Tap My Friends, Except under the Who Can See My Location section.
  3. Select the accounts you want to turn off location sharing for, then tap Save.

Method 3: Disable Snapchat Location Access From Phone Settings

While Ghost Mode hides your location from friends, Snapchat can still access location data internally. To completely turn off location on Snapchat, you need to change your device’s permissions.

On iPhone:

  1. Go to Settings → Apps → Snapchat.
  2. Tap Location.
  3. Select Never under Allow Location Access.

Also Read: How to Change Your Location on an iPhone

On Android:

  1. Go to Settings → Apps → Snapchat.
  2. Tap Permissions → Location.
  3. Select Don’t Allow under Location access for this app.

Does Snapchat Track Your Location When the App Is Closed?

No, Snapchat does not actively update or share your live location while the app is closed. Your location on Snap Map updates only when you open and use Snapchat.

When you leave the app, your last known location may remain visible to friends for a few hours. After a period of inactivity, Snapchat automatically removes your location from the map until you reopen the app.

Keep in mind that this also depends on your phone’s location permissions. If location access is set to Always, Snapchat can access location data at the system level, but your Snap Map location still refreshes primarily when the app is in use. Setting location permission to Never completely prevents Snapchat from accessing your location.

What Happens When You Turn Off Location on Snapchat?

When location sharing is disabled:

  • Your Bitmoji disappears from Snap Map.
  • Friends cannot track your real-time location.
  • You can still view the map and stories.
  • Snapchat stops updating your visible location on the Snap Map.

Summing Up

Turning off your location on Snapchat takes only a few seconds once you know where to look. Enabling Ghost Mode instantly hides your location, while device-level permissions let you control how much data Snapchat can access.

Have more Snapchat privacy questions? Ask them in the comments section.

FAQs

Will friends know if I turn off my location?

No. Snapchat does not notify others when you enable Ghost Mode or turn off location sharing with them.

Can Snapchat still see my location?

Yes, unless you revoke location permissions from your phone settings.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: macOS Will Flag the Slower USB-C Port on MacBook Neo

content.rendered:
Apple has equipped the new MacBook Neo with two USB-C ports, but they are not identical in terms of functionality and performance. While the laptop may appear to have symmetrical connectivity, the capabilities of each port differ significantly.

The USB-C port on the left side supports USB 3 speeds up to 10 Gbps. This faster port is designed for high-bandwidth tasks, such as connecting external SSDs, docks, and displays.

Meanwhile, the USB-C port located closer to the trackpad, is limited to USB 2 speeds of just 480 Mbps. This makes it suitable for charging and basic accessories, but it cannot handle more demanding connections.

External Display Works Only Through One Port

Due to this hardware limitation, Apple confirms that external display connectivity is supported only through the left USB-C port. Attempting to connect a monitor through the slower right side port will not work for display output.

Apple says the MacBook Neo supports one external display with up to 4K resolution at 60 Hz, allowing users to extend their workspace to a larger screen.

macOS Warns If You Use the Wrong Port

Since the ports are not labeled on the MacBook Neo, users could easily plug an external display into the wrong port.

However, according to Daring Fireball’s John Gruber, macOS helps reduce this confusion. If you connect a display to the slower USB 2 port, the system shows a notification informing you that the display must be connected to the other port.

Pricing and Availability

The MacBook Neo is currently available to pre-order in the United States, starting at $599. Apple also offers a $499 price for college students, making it the most affordable MacBook in the company’s lineup.

The laptop is scheduled to officially launch on March 11.

Would this USB-C port limitation affect your buying decision? Let us know in the comments.

Read more: macOS 27: What to expect from Apple’s next Mac update

excerpt.rendered: The MacBook Neo includes two USB-C ports with different capabilities. The left port supports faster speeds and external displays, while the right port is limited to USB 2 speeds for charging and basic accessories.
