title.rendered: How to Set Up an Apple Recovery Key: A Complete Guide

content.rendered:
If you use Apple devices, you already know your Apple Account sits at the center of your digital life. It unlocks your iPhone, backs up your photos, secures your messages, syncs your passwords, and gives you access to services like Apple Music, iCloud, and FaceTime.

So when you cannot sign in because you forgot your password, got locked out, or lost your device, everything suddenly feels fragile. Apple’s standard recovery process works, but it can take several days. That is not ideal when you need immediate access. That is exactly where an Apple Recovery Key comes in.

This guide explains what a recovery key is, why you might want one, and how to set it up on your Apple devices.

Table of Contents
  • What is an Apple Recovery Key?
  • Standard Recovery vs. Recovery Key: What’s the Difference?
  • Why You Should Enable an Apple Recovery Key
  • How to Set Up an Apple Recovery Key on iPhone or iPad
  • How to Set Up an Apple Recovery Key on Mac
  • How to Create a New Recovery Key
  • How to Use an Apple Recovery Key
  • How to Remove an Apple Recovery Key
  • Apple Recovery Key and Advanced Data Protection
  • Final Thoughts

What is an Apple Recovery Key?

An Apple Recovery Key is a 28-character, randomly generated code that serves as a backup method to regain access to your account if something goes wrong.

There is an important tradeoff. When you enable a recovery key, you turn off Apple’s standard account recovery methods.

If you lose access to your devices and also lose your recovery key, you will be permanently locked out of your account. Apple cannot restore access. This feature offers powerful protection, but it requires careful handling.

Standard Recovery vs. Recovery Key: What’s the Difference?

Why You Should Enable an Apple Recovery Key

Once enabled, the recovery key becomes one of the only ways to reset your Apple Account password.

Here is why that matters:

  • Greater control over account recovery: You rely on your recovery key and trusted phone number rather than Apple’s extended verification process.
  • Stronger security protection: If someone tries to take over your account, they cannot reset your password without the recovery key, even if they have your device or password.

How to Set Up an Apple Recovery Key on iPhone or iPad

Before setting up your recovery key, make sure you meet the following two requirements:

  • Your device is running iOS 14 or later, iPadOS 14 or later, or macOS Big Sur or later.
  • Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) is enabled.

Steps to Set It Up

  1. Open Settings and tap your Apple Account name at the top.
  2. Tap Sign-In & Security.
  3. Select the Recovery Key. You will see an introduction and a warning about setting up the Recovery Key.
  4. Tap Continue > Use Recovery Key. Apple warns you that standard account recovery will be disabled.
  5. Authenticate with Face ID, Touch ID, or your passcode.
  6. Your 28-character recovery key appears. This step is critical. Write it down. Print it. Store it somewhere secure. Do not take a screenshot. Apple will not display it again after setup.
  7. Tap Continue and re-enter the key to confirm.

Once verified, your recovery key is active.

How to Set Up an Apple Recovery Key on Mac

If you are using macOS Sonoma or later:

  1. Open System Settings and click your Apple Account name.
  2. Select Sign-In & Security, then click Recovery Key.
  3. A pop-up will appear. Click Turn On, and another pop-up will appear with a warning; click Use Recovery Key.
  4. Enter your Mac administrator password and hit Allow.
  5. There’s your Recovery Key. Print it or write it down, again, no screenshots, no keeping it in iCloud.
  6. Enter the recovery key you just wrote down for verification. Once you click Done, the setup is complete. You will be redirected to the recovery key setup page.

How to Create a New Recovery Key

If you lose your recovery key but still have access to a trusted device, you can replace it.

On iPhone or iPad:

  1. Go to Settings > Apple Account Name > Sign-In & Security.
  2. Tap Recovery Key.
  3. You will see the Recovery Key setup page with remove and replace key options. Tap Replace Recovery Key.
  4. Again, tap Replace Recovery Key in the pop-up box, and follow the same steps to verify.

On Mac:

  1. Go to System Settings and select Sign-In & Security, same as the previous steps.
  2. Click the Recovery Key. A pop-up with setup options will appear.
  3. Click Create New, enter Mac admin password.
  4. Read the warning about the Forgot recovery key and then hit Replace Recovery Key.
  5. Your new key will appear. Again, write it down. This replaces your old key, making the old one invalid.

How to Use an Apple Recovery Key

If you forget your Apple Account password:

Apple will ask for:

  • Your 28-character recovery key
  • A verification code was sent to your trusted phone number
  • Enter both to regain access immediately.

This bypasses the multi-day account recovery process entirely.

How to Remove an Apple Recovery Key

If you decide you no longer want to use a recovery key:

  1. Go to Settings > Apple Account Name > Sign-In & Security.
  2. Tap Recovery Key.
  3. On the setup screen, tap Remove Recovery Key. Enter the Passcode and confirm.

Your key has been removed.

Apple Recovery Key and Advanced Data Protection

Advanced Data Protection is Apple’s highest level of iCloud security. When enabled, most iCloud data becomes end-to-end encrypted. Only you can decrypt it. Apple cannot access or recover that data.

To enable Advanced Data Protection, Apple requires at least one recovery method:

  • A Recovery Key
  • A Recovery Contact

You can enable both for additional flexibility.

Final Thoughts

Setting up an Apple Recovery Key may feel intimidating at first, but it is one of the strongest steps you can take to protect your account.

For most users, enabling a recovery key makes sense, as long as you store it securely and understand the responsibility involved. Treat it like a physical safe key. If it is lost, access may be gone for good.

FAQs

Do I need a trusted device to set up a recovery key?

Yes. A trusted iPhone, iPad, or Mac signed in to your Apple Account is required to create or update a recovery key.

What happens if I lose my Apple Recovery Key?

If you still have access to a trusted device, you can generate a new key. If you lose both your trusted devices and your recovery key, your Apple Account may become permanently inaccessible.

Can I view my Apple Recovery Key again after I set it up?

No. Apple displays it only once during setup.

Where should I store my recovery key safely?

Use a secure offline method such as:

  • A written note stored in a safe place
  • An encrypted USB drive
  • A trusted password manager

Avoid storing it in iCloud Photos, Notes, or iCloud Drive.

Can one recovery key work across all devices?

Yes. One recovery key applies to every device signed in to your Apple Account.

Is a recovery key required for Advanced Data Protection?

Not specifically. However, you must choose at least one recovery method, either a Recovery Key or a Recovery Contact, to enable Advanced Data Protection.

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Apple Pay requires authentication through Face ID, Touch ID, or the device passcode. Without this verification, payments cannot be completed.

mainEntity.name: Does disabling Apple Pay cancel your physical cards?

mainEntity.name: Do I need a trusted device to set up a recovery key?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A trusted iPhone, iPad, or Mac signed in to your Apple Account is required to create or update a recovery key.

mainEntity.name: What happens if I lose my Apple Recovery Key?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you still have access to a trusted device, you can generate a new key. If you lose both your trusted devices and your recovery key, your Apple Account may become permanently inaccessible.

mainEntity.name: Can I view my Apple Recovery Key again after I set it up?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Apple displays it only once during setup.

mainEntity.name: Where should I store my recovery key safely?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use a secure offline method such as: A written note stored in a safe place An encrypted USB drive A trusted password manager Avoid storing it in iCloud Photos, Notes, or iCloud Drive.

mainEntity.name: Can one recovery key work across all devices?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. One recovery key applies to every device signed in to your Apple Account.

mainEntity.name: Is a recovery key required for Advanced Data Protection?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not specifically. However, you must choose at least one recovery method, either a Recovery Key or a Recovery Contact, to enable Advanced Data Protection.

title.rendered: Apple Aims to Keep iPhone 18 Pro Starting Prices in Line With iPhone 17 Pro

content.rendered:
Apple is working to keep the starting prices of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max at roughly the same level as the current iPhone 17 Pro models, according to supply chain research shared by equity analyst Jeff Pu of GF Securities.

In the U.S., the iPhone 17 Pro starts at $1,099 and the iPhone 17 Pro Max starts at $1,199. Apple’s goal for the next generation is to keep pricing either unchanged or at a similar level, despite rising component costs.

Apple Is Focusing on Cost Control to Offset Rising Memory Prices

Behind the scenes, Apple is prioritizing cost management as DRAM and NAND storage prices climb sharply. The company has reportedly been negotiating with major memory suppliers Samsung and SK Hynix to secure more favorable pricing on chips.

Memory is one of the most expensive components inside a modern smartphone. Rising DRAM and NAND costs can significantly affect overall device pricing, especially for high-end models with large storage tiers.

Apple is also expected to look for savings in other core components, including display panels and camera systems, in order to balance its bill of materials without pushing retail prices higher.

Analysts Expect Flat Pricing Strategy for the Pro Line

Industry analyst Ming-Chi Kuo has similarly indicated that Apple plans to avoid price increases for the iPhone 18 Pro models as much as possible. That suggests the company is attempting to preserve its current premium pricing structure rather than testing higher entry points.

If Apple succeeds, the iPhone 18 Pro lineup would maintain a starting price of $1,099, with the Pro Max beginning at $1,199 in the U.S., matching the previous generation.

Apple is expected to unveil the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max in September.

excerpt.rendered: Apple plans to keep iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max prices flat with the iPhone 17 Pro, managing rising memory and component costs ahead of a September launch.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A trusted iPhone, iPad, or Mac signed in to your Apple Account is required to create or update a recovery key.

title.rendered: How to Recover Deleted Call History on iPhone

content.rendered:
Accidentally deleting call history is more common than people admit. You open the Phone app to find a number or confirm a call, and it is no longer there. This can be stressful, especially when the call was important. The good news is that deleted call history on an iPhone is not always permanently gone. In many cases, it can still be recovered if you know where to look and act in time.

This article explains all the practical ways to recover deleted call history on an iPhone.

Table of Contents
  • Can You Really Recover Deleted Call History on iPhone?
  • Method 1: Recover Deleted Call History Using iCloud Backup
  • Method 2: Recover Call History Using Finder or iTunes Backup
  • Method 3: Recover Deleted Call History Without Backup Using Recovery Tools
  • Method 4: Request a Copy of Your Data From Apple
  • Method 5: Check Call History From Your Mobile Carrier
  • Comparison: Which Recovery Method Is Right for You?
  • Important Things to Know Before Recovering Call History
  • Final Thoughts

Can You Really Recover Deleted Call History on iPhone?

Yes, in many situations, recovery is possible. When you delete a call log, the iPhone does not remove it instantly. The data stays hidden until new data overwrites it. Recovery mainly depends on how recently the call was deleted and whether a backup or external record exists.

Apple supports recovery through backups, mobile carriers store call records independently, and recovery tools may scan the device before data is overwritten. Each option works differently, so choosing the right one matters.

Method 1: Recover Deleted Call History Using iCloud Backup

If iCloud backup is enabled on your iPhone, this is the most reliable and Apple-supported method. iCloud automatically backs up call history along with other phone data.

This method helps when you have enabled iCloud backup and you are sure the backup was created before the call history was removed. However, restoring an iCloud backup replaces all current data on your iPhone, and you cannot restore only call history.

  1. Open the Settings app and go to General.
  2. Tap Transfer or Reset iPhone, then select Erase All Content and Settings.
  3. Tap Continue and enter your iPhone passcode.
  4. When asked to back up, tap Skip Backup.
  5. Now we need to set up the iPhone from scratch
  6. Follow the setup process until you reach the Apps & Data screen.
  7. Select Restore from iCloud Backup.
  8. Sign in with your Apple ID.
  9. Choose a backup created before the call history was deleted.

After the restore completes, open the Phone app and check the Recents tab. If the backup contains your deleted calls, they should now be visible.

Method 2: Recover Call History Using Finder or iTunes Backup

If you previously backed up your iPhone to a computer, you can restore that backup to recover deleted call logs. Finder is used on macOS Catalina and later, while iTunes is used on older Macs and Windows PCs. This method restores the entire backup and overwrites current data similar to the previous process.

  1. Connect your iPhone to your computer using a cable.
  2. Unlock your iPhone and tap Trust if prompted.
  3. Open Finder or iTunes.
  4. Select your iPhone from the sidebar or device list.
  5. Click Restore Backup.
  6. Choose a backup created before the call history was deleted.
  7. Click Erase and Restore to confirm your decision and start the process.

Once completed, open the Phone app and check your call history. If the selected backup included the missing call logs, they should now be restored. This option is useful if you regularly back up your iPhone to a computer. Remember, data created after the backup will be lost, similar to the previous process.

Also check out: How to Restore iPhone from Backup for a more detailed guide.

Method 3: Recover Deleted Call History Without Backup Using Recovery Tools

If you do not have an iCloud or computer backup, recovery becomes more time-sensitive. Deleted call logs may still exist inside the iPhone database until new data overwrites them. Some recovery tools scan the iPhone directly and attempt to locate deleted call records, sometimes allowing selective recovery without resetting the device.

Use caution with these tools. They require deep access to your device, and not all of them respect user privacy. Choose reputable software only. This approach works best when the deletion happened recently and the phone has not been heavily used since.

These tools are usually run from a Windows PC or Mac and work by scanning for fragments of deleted data, giving you a chance to preview and recover specific items.

Here are some tools that many users try:

  1. PhoneRescue for iOS – A popular recovery tool that scans both the device and backups. It lets you preview deleted data and recover just the call logs you need.
  2. iMyFone D-Back – Known for its ability to preview call history before recovery and retrieve deleted logs without affecting current data.
  3. Syncios Data Recovery – Another tool that lets you scan your iPhone directly for lost call logs and other deleted data.

Method 4: Request a Copy of Your Data From Apple

Apple allows users to request a copy of personal data associated with their Apple ID, which may include call history. This method does not erase your device, but it can take several days.

  1. Visit Apple’s Data and Privacy page in a browser.
  2. Sign in with your Apple ID and complete two-factor authentication.
  3. Select Request a copy of your data.
  4. Choose the data categories you want to download.
  5. Select a file size and submit the request.

Apple will notify you by email when the data is ready. Once downloaded, you can review the file to check whether your call history is included. This method is slower, but it is safe and officially supported by Apple.

Method 5: Check Call History From Your Mobile Carrier

Mobile carriers store call records for billing and account purposes, often for several months. You can check these by logging into your carrier’s website or app, where call dates, numbers, and durations may be listed.

If the information is not visible, you can contact carrier support and request it directly. Carrier records cannot restore call history to your iPhone, but they can help recover important details. This option is especially helpful when you only need call dates, numbers, or durations.

Comparison: Which Recovery Method Is Right for You?

At this point, you may be wondering which method makes the most sense for your situation. The right choice depends on whether you have a backup, how quickly you need the information, and whether you are comfortable resetting your iPhone. The table below gives a quick comparison to help you decide.

Important Things to Know Before Recovering Call History

Before you start trying to recover deleted call history, it helps to understand a few practical limitations and realities. These points set clear expectations and can save you time, effort, and unnecessary data loss.

  • Recovery depends on how recently the call history was deleted.
  • Restoring from backups replaces current data.
  • Deleted calls become unrecoverable once overwritten.
  • Recovery tools may help but require privacy awareness.
  • Carriers often store call records longer than iPhones.

Final Thoughts

Deleting call history by mistake can feel frustrating, especially when the call matters. In most cases, there is still a way to retrieve the information. Whether you use an iCloud backup, a computer backup, Apple’s data request option, or your carrier’s records, each method offers a possible solution. Choose the option that best fits your situation and act as soon as possible. With the right approach, lost call history does not always stay lost.

title.rendered: How to Download iOS Update Using Cellular Data on iPhone

content.rendered:
Updating your iPhone to the latest iOS version is important for security, performance, and new features. Normally, Apple recommends downloading iOS updates over Wi-Fi because the update files are large. However, there are situations where Wi-Fi isn’t available or too slow, and you may want to update your iPhone using cellular data instead.

In this guide, you’ll learn how to download over-the-air iOS updates using mobile data on iPhone or iPad, when it works, and what to do if the option doesn’t appear.

Table of Contents
  • Can You Update Your iPhone Over Cellular Data?
  • How to Download an iOS Update Using Mobile Data
  • Important Things to Know About Updating Over Cellular
  • What to Do If You Can’t Download iOS Updates Using Cellular Data
  • Alternative Method: Use Personal Hotspot
  • Final Thoughts

Can You Update Your iPhone Over Cellular Data?

Yes, newer iPhones running iOS 15 or later allow you to download iOS updates over the air using cellular data, especially on 5G connections and when certain settings are enabled.

Apple added this flexibility so users can update their devices even when Wi-Fi isn’t available. This is especially useful when you begin downloading an iOS update using Wi-Fi but lose connection in the middle. The download will resume over the cellular connection.

How to Download an iOS Update Using Mobile Data

If Wi-Fi isn’t available, follow these methods to install over-the-air iPhone software updates. If you have an iPhone that supports 5G (iPhone 12 or later), you can install the iOS update via cellular data without employing any workarounds.

  1. Simply, go to Settings > General > Software Update.
  2. Your iPhone will check for available updates. Tap Download & Install to start downloading.
  3. If your iPhone is disconnected from Wi-Fi, it will show a dialogue box asking for cellular data permission.
  4. Tap Continue, and the download will resume.

Ensure you have an active cellular plan. These same steps will also be applicable for 4G, LTE, or 3G networks.

However, sometimes it gets restricted due to data limits and carrier settings. To download a large file, all you need to do is:

  1. Open Settings and go to Cellular.
  2. Toggle on Cellular Data and tap Cellular Data Options. On dual-SIM iPhones, you must select a SIM to get these options.
  3. Now, select Data Mode and choose Allow More Data on 5G.

This will allow iOS updates, automatic iCloud backups, and FaceTime in higher quality over cellular. Now, try installing the update again.

Note

You may hit your monthly data allowance and face extra data charges. You can also turn off cellular data for specific apps to save mobile data and use it later.

Important Things to Know About Updating Over Cellular

Before downloading an iOS update using cellular data, there are a few important things you should keep in mind to avoid interruptions or unexpected data usage.

  • iOS Updates Are Large: Most iOS updates are between 1 GB and 6 GB. Make sure your cellular plan can handle it.
  • Battery Level Matters: Your iPhone usually requires 50% battery or to be plugged into a charger.
  • 4G vs 5G Limitations: Cellular updates are more reliable on 5G networks. Some carriers may restrict large downloads on 4G/LTE.
  • Network Stability: If your cellular signal drops during the download, the update may pause or fail.
  • Download Speed May Be Slower: Cellular downloads can take longer than Wi-Fi, depending on signal strength. You may use some workarounds to boost cellular speed.

Taking a moment to check these factors can help ensure your iOS update installs smoothly without interruptions.

What to Do If You Can’t Download iOS Updates Using Cellular Data

If your iPhone won’t download the iOS update, don’t worry! A few simple checks can usually fix the issue.

  • Restart your iPhone: A quick restart can resolve temporary network or system glitches that may prevent the update from downloading.
  • Check available storage: iOS updates require enough free space to download and install. Go to Settings > General > iPhone Storage and free up space if needed.
  • Update carrier settings: Sometimes carrier configuration updates are required for cellular downloads to work properly. Open Settings > General > About and install any available carrier updates.
  • Ensure cellular data is enabled from Settings > Cellular.
  • Reset network settings if needed. Go to Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Reset > Reset Network Settings. This will remove saved Wi-Fi passwords.

Temporary carrier restrictions or weak signal strength can block large downloads. Moving to a location with better coverage or trying again later may help.

If it still doesn’t work, Apple may be restricting downloads based on region, carrier rules, or network type. In that case, contact Apple Support for the best solution.

Alternative Method: Use Personal Hotspot

If cellular updates are blocked, you can:

  • Connect to another phone’s hotspot
  • Use a portable Wi-Fi device
  • Visit a public Wi-Fi location

Your iPhone treats hotspot connections as Wi-Fi. If nothing works, update your iPhone manually using your Mac or PC.

Final Thoughts 

Downloading an iOS update using cellular data can be a convenient option when Wi-Fi isn’t available. With the right settings enabled and a stable mobile connection, you can keep your iPhone updated without waiting to connect to a wireless network.

Just remember to check your data limit, battery level, and storage space before starting the update to avoid interruptions. Stay updated, stay secure, and make the most of your iPhone!

FAQs

Can I update iOS without Wi-Fi? 

Yes, newer iPhones support iOS updates over cellular data, especially on 5G networks. 

Why won’t my iPhone update using mobile data? 

Possible reasons include data restrictions, unsupported iOS version, carrier limitations, and low storage. 

Does updating iOS use a lot of data? 

Yes. A full iOS update can use several gigabytes of data.

title.rendered: ChatGPT Begins Showing Ads to Free and Go Tier Users in the U.S.

content.rendered:
OpenAI has started displaying ads inside ChatGPT for users on its Free and Go subscription plans in the United States. The change takes effect today and represents a major shift in how the company supports the cost of operating its AI chatbot.

Ads are limited to logged-in adult users. OpenAI says minors will not be shown advertising.

Ads Are Meant to Fund ChatGPT’s Rising Infrastructure Costs

According to OpenAI, operating ChatGPT requires significant infrastructure and ongoing investment, and the company is not yet profitable. Ads are being introduced to help fund the free and low-cost tiers without removing access entirely.

Users who prefer not to see ads can upgrade to paid plans such as Plus or Pro. OpenAI is also offering an option to disable ads in exchange for fewer daily free messages.

Sponsored Content Will Be Clearly Labeled and Separated From Answers

OpenAI says ads will be clearly marked as sponsored and displayed separately from ChatGPT’s responses. The company states that advertising will not influence the answers the chatbot provides.

Ads may be selected based on factors like conversation topics, previous chats, and past ad interactions. Advertisers will only receive aggregated data, such as views or clicks, and will not have access to chat history, stored memories, or personal user information.

Sensitive Topics Will Remain Ad-Free

Ads will not appear in conversations related to sensitive subjects, including health, mental health, or politics. OpenAI says this restriction is designed to protect users and maintain trust in high-stakes discussions.

Also read: Open announces ChatGPT Health.

Users will be able to dismiss ads, provide feedback, see why an ad is being shown, delete ad data, and disable ad personalization entirely.

Paid ChatGPT Plans Will Continue to Offer an Ad-Free Experience

Subscribers on Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Education plans will not see ads. OpenAI says the current rollout is a test phase aimed at learning from user feedback and refining how ads work inside ChatGPT.

The move comes at a time of increasing competition in the AI chatbot space, with rivals positioning themselves around different business models. For OpenAI, ads represent a calculated step toward sustainability while trying to preserve user trust.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A trusted iPhone, iPad, or Mac signed in to your Apple Account is required to create or update a recovery key.

acceptedAnswer.text: If you still have access to a trusted device, you can generate a new key. If you lose both your trusted devices and your recovery key, your Apple Account may become permanently inaccessible.

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Apple displays it only once during setup.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. One recovery key applies to every device signed in to your Apple Account.

title.rendered: WhatsApp Web Is Finally Getting Voice and Video Calls

content.rendered:
After years of being limited to messaging only, WhatsApp Web is starting to support voice and video calls. The long-awaited feature is now rolling out to some users, as first reported by WABetaInfo, marking a major step forward for the browser version of the popular messaging service.

This update brings WhatsApp Web closer to feature parity with its mobile and desktop apps, which have supported calling for years.

Calls Are Rolling Out First to Beta Users

Voice and video calling on WhatsApp Web is currently available to users enrolled in the platform’s beta program. The rollout has started gradually, and more users are expected to gain access over the coming weeks.

At this stage, the feature is limited to one-on-one conversations. Users can place calls directly from their browser without downloading or installing a desktop app. Once enabled, the calling option appears inside individual chats, making it easy to start a voice or video call in just a few clicks.

How Calling Works on WhatsApp Web

Using calls on WhatsApp Web feels familiar. The interface closely matches what users already see on the Windows and Mac desktop apps. From a chat window, users can start either a voice call or a video call using the call controls at the top of the screen.

Video calls also support screen sharing. This allows users to show documents, presentations, or other on-screen content during a call. The experience is designed to be simple and consistent with WhatsApp’s existing calling tools.

Security Stays the Same as on Mobile

Calls made through WhatsApp Web are protected with end-to-end encryption. The same security model used on mobile devices and desktop apps applies here as well.

This encryption relies on the Signal protocol, which ensures that only the people on the call can hear or see the conversation. Neither WhatsApp nor its parent company Meta can access the content of these calls. No special settings are required, as encryption is enabled by default.

Group Calls Are Coming Later

Group voice and video calls are still under development for WhatsApp Web. When they do arrive, they are expected to support up to 32 participants, along with features like call links and scheduled calls.

For now, WhatsApp appears to be focusing on stability and performance before expanding calling support to group chats. This phased approach helps ensure the web experience matches the reliability users expect.

A Big Win for Web and Linux Users

The addition of calling is especially important for users who rely heavily on WhatsApp Web. This includes people on systems where official desktop apps are limited or unavailable.

With voice and video calls now possible directly in the browser, WhatsApp Web becomes a much more complete communication tool. It no longer feels like a stripped-down companion to the mobile app, but a fully capable platform in its own right.

As the rollout continues beyond beta users, WhatsApp Web calling is set to become a standard part of how millions of people stay connected online.

mainEntity.name: Can I view my Apple Recovery Key again after I set it up?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Apple displays it only once during setup.

mainEntity.name: Where should I store my recovery key safely?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use a secure offline method such as: A written note stored in a safe place An encrypted USB drive A trusted password manager Avoid storing it in iCloud Photos, Notes, or iCloud Drive.

mainEntity.name: Can one recovery key work across all devices?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. One recovery key applies to every device signed in to your Apple Account.

acceptedAnswer.text: Not specifically. However, you must choose at least one recovery method, either a Recovery Key or a Recovery Contact, to enable Advanced Data Protection.

title.rendered: Best Audiobook Apps for iPhone and Android You Should Try

content.rendered:
Audiobooks have become one of the easiest ways to enjoy books in today’s busy world. The audiobook apps let you listen to stories and learn new things without needing to sit down and read. They offer smart features like offline listening, AI-powered narration, and seamless syncing across devices.

In this guide, we’ll explore the best audiobook apps you can use on your iPhone and Android based on usability, features, and value.

Table of Contents
  • How We Tested the Audiobook Apps
  • These Are the Best Audiobook Apps for iOS and Android
    • 1. Audible
    • 2. Libby
    • 3. Hoopla Digital
    • 4. Audiobooks.com
    • 5. Google Play Books
    • 6. LibriVox Audiobooks
    • 7. Storytel
    • Subscription vs Pay-Per-Book: Which Is Better in 2026?
    • Features to Look for in an Audiobook App
    • Are Free Audiobook Apps Worth It?
    • Final Verdict

How We Tested the Audiobook Apps

To make this guide practical and useful, we tested the most popular audiobook apps using our strict review guidelines and real-world listening scenarios.

  • Platform Compatibility: All apps were tested on both iOS and Android devices to ensure consistent performance across platforms.
  • Subscription vs Free Apps: We evaluated free, subscription-based, and pay-per-book platforms. This helps different types of listeners choose the right option.
  • Audio Quality Testing: Narration clarity, streaming quality, playback controls, etc., are important. Apps with clear narration and smooth playback controls ranked higher.
  • Offline Playback Performance: Offline listening is essential for commuters and travelers. We tested download speed, storage handling, and playback reliability without the internet.
  • UI/UX Evaluation: Apps that required fewer taps to start listening scored better. This includes ease of finding books, library organization, player interface, and recommendation system.
  • Library Size and Pricing Comparison: We compared the total audiobook catalog. pricing models, and free vs premium content availability.

These Are the Best Audiobook Apps for iOS and Android

Below are the top audiobook apps, ranked by usability, features, and value.

1. Audible

Audible remains the most complete audiobook platform in 2026. It offers a massive audiobook library, exclusive titles, podcasts, and strong app performance. You will find an audiobook from almost every genre and mood.

The app’s AI-powered recommendations and seamless device syncing make it ideal for regular listeners. Moreover, offline downloads and CarPlay/Apple Watch streaming work reliably, and narration quality is consistently excellent.

Audible is best for people who listen to multiple audiobooks every month and want premium content.

Download: iPhone | Android

2. Libby

Libby connects directly to public libraries, allowing users to borrow audiobooks for free using a library card. The app’s interface is simple, and downloads work well for offline listening.

You can adjust speed from 0.6-3x, set a sleep timer, and add bookmarks, notes, and highlights during the playback. While availability depends on your local library, Libby is one of the best free audiobook solutions available.

Ideal for budget-conscious listeners and students.

Download: iPhone | Android

3. Hoopla Digital

Hoopla Digital is another library-based audiobook platform, but it focuses on instant borrowing rather than waitlists. You can access up to 1.5 million audiobooks collection with a single BingePass and your library card.

It also includes movies, comics, manga, TV shows, and music, making it a multi-media borrowing app. Cross-device syncing and offline listening works smoothly, though monthly borrowing limits apply.

Best for users who want free audiobooks without long holds.

Download: iPhone | Android

4. Audiobooks.com

Audiobooks.com offers a subscription model similar to Audible but with a simpler interface and flexible pricing. It has half a million audiobooks with more than ten thousand free titles.

You can find kids’ stories, meditation titles, calming soundscapes, crime & thrillers, and much more. Additionally, the app includes offline listening, sleep timer, curated recommendations, and unique features and bonuses for paid members.

A good alternative for users who want a straightforward audiobook subscription service.

Download: iPhone | Android

5. Google Play Books

Google Play Books uses a pay-per-book model, meaning there’s no subscription required. All you need to do is find your preferred audiobook and purchase it. The app also lets you share your purchased titles with your family members.

Along with the basic features, you can control audiobooks hands-free with Siri. Google Play Books is ideal for occasional listeners who only want to buy specific audiobooks. The app’s syncing across Android devices is excellent.

Best for casual audiobook listeners.

Download: iPhone | Android

6. LibriVox Audiobooks

LibriVox offers free public-domain audiobooks, mostly classic literature. It has 45,000+ bestseller titles in 30+ languages for free. You can stream unlimited novels, history, poetry, etc. The best part is that you can find out-of-print books here.

Narration quality varies because recordings are volunteer-based, but the app is simple and lightweight. Simply start listening, pause, and pick up where you left off later.

Best for classic book lovers and free audiobook listeners.

Download: iPhone | Android

7. Storytel

Storytel offers unlimited audiobook listening through a subscription model. You can access more than 1 million titles and follow your favorite authors and series for new updates. The app lets you switch between listening and reading instantly, set a listening goal, and shows your stats.

It’s especially strong in regional content, in-depth podcasts, multilingual audiobooks, and exclusive Storytel Originals. The app performs well offline and includes smart recommendations and trending lists.

Best for international audiobook listeners.

Download: iPhone | Android

Subscription vs Pay-Per-Book: Which Is Better in 2026?

Your listening habits determine the best option.

A subscription model works best if you:

  • Listen to multiple audiobooks monthly
  • Explore new genres often
  • Prefer unlimited listening

A pay-per-book model is better if you:

  • Listen occasionally
  • Want to own audiobooks permanently
  • Prefer no monthly commitment

In 2026, subscriptions generally provide better value for frequent listeners, while pay-per-book remains ideal for casual users.

Features to Look for in an Audiobook App

When choosing an audiobook app, focus on usability features that improve the listening experience.

Important features include:

  • Sleep timer
  • Playback speed control
  • Offline downloads
  • Cross-platform sync
  • AI narration support
  • Smart recommendations
  • CarPlay / Android Auto support

These features make daily listening more convenient and flexible.

Are Free Audiobook Apps Worth It?

Yes, but with limitations.

Free audiobook apps usually:

  • Have smaller libraries
  • Focus on classics or library borrowing
  • Include waitlists or borrowing limits

However, they’re excellent for students, casual listeners, budget users, and classic literature fans.

For heavy listeners looking for unique titles or specific tastes, paid apps still provide the best experience.

Final Verdict

Audiobook apps in 2026 are smarter, faster, and more accessible than ever. The right app depends on how you listen.

  • If you want the largest catalog and premium experience, Audible is still the best choice.
  • For free audiobooks, Libby and Hoopla are excellent options.
  • If you want flexibility without subscriptions, Google Play Books is a strong alternative.

Overall, audiobook apps have become a core part of digital reading, and choosing the right one can completely change how you enjoy books.

FAQs

Can I listen to audiobooks offline?

Yes. Most audiobook apps allow you to download audiobooks for offline listening.

Which audiobook app has the largest library?

Audible currently has the largest commercial audiobook library.

Are audiobooks cheaper than eBooks?

Not usually. Audiobooks are often more expensive due to narration production costs, but subscription services reduce the price per book.

  • Best iPhone Lock Screen Widgets
  • Best Safari Extensions for iPhone and iPad

blockGraphs.answer: Yes. Most audiobook apps allow you to download audiobooks for offline listening.

blockGraphs.question: Which audiobook app has the largest library?
blockGraphs.answer: Audible currently has the largest commercial audiobook library.

blockGraphs.question: Are audiobooks cheaper than eBooks?
blockGraphs.answer: Not usually. Audiobooks are often more expensive due to narration production costs, but subscription services reduce the price per book.

title.rendered: Forgot Apple Watch Passcode? How to Reset and Unlock It

content.rendered:
You probably don’t forget your Apple Watch passcode easily. You wear the watch on your wrist every day, unlock it multiple times, and the muscle memory sticks. That makes forgetting the passcode feel unlikely, but it can still happen. A long break from wearing the watch, a recent passcode change, or too many incorrect attempts can completely lock you out.

When that happens, it quickly becomes frustrating because there is no way to retrieve or view the forgotten passcode. The only fix is to erase the Apple Watch and set it up again. Keep reading to learn how to reset your Apple Watch passcode with or without the paired iPhone.

Table of Contents
  • What Happens When You Reset an Apple Watch
  • Method 1: Reset Apple Watch Using a Paired iPhone
  • Method 2: Reset Apple Watch Without iPhone
  • How to Restore Apple Watch Data After Reset
  • Can You Reset Apple Watch Without Apple ID or Password?
  • Apple Watch Reset Not Working? Common Issues and Fixes
  • Tips to Avoid Forgetting Your Apple Watch Passcode Again
  • Summing Up…

What Happens When You Reset an Apple Watch

Before you reset the watch, it’s important to understand what happens next. Resetting does more than remove the passcode. It completely erases the device and prepares it for a fresh setup.

When the reset is complete, the following changes take place:

  • All data, apps, and settings are permanently deleted from the watch.
  • The passcode is removed and cannot be recovered.
  • The watch disconnects from your iPhone.
  • You must pair the Apple Watch again during setup.
  • Activation Lock may require your Apple ID and password.
  • Health and Activity data can be restored only if a backup exists.

If you reset your Apple Watch via the Watch app on your iPhone, a backup is automatically created during unpairing. This allows you to restore apps, watch faces, and settings after the reset.

However, if the reset is performed directly on the Apple Watch, no new backup is created during the process. The watch can still be restored from an existing iPhone backup if one is available. If no backup exists, the watch must be set up as new, and previously stored data cannot be recovered.

Method 1: Reset Apple Watch Using a Paired iPhone

This is the preferred way to reset an Apple Watch because the unpairing process creates a fresh backup and removes Activation Lock after you confirm with your Apple Account during the reset.

  1. Open the Watch app on your paired iPhone and ensure you are on the “My Watch” tab.
  2. Tap the All Watches button at the top left corner.
  3. Tap the i (Information) button next to the Apple Watch you want to reset.
  4. Here, scroll to the bottom and tap Unpair Apple Watch.
  5. Next, tap Unpair [Your Name] Apple Watch on the confirmation prompt.
  6. Finally, enter your Apple Account (formerly Apple ID) password to finish resetting.

Your iPhone creates a fresh backup and erases the watch. Once done, bring the iPhone near the watch and follow the pairing instructions. Choose Restore from Backup when asked.

Method 2: Reset Apple Watch Without iPhone

Use this method when the paired iPhone is not available.

  1. Connect your Apple Watch to its charger.
  2. Now, press and hold the Side button until the Emergency Call screen appears.
  3. Next, press and hold the Digital Crown until the “Erase all content and settings?” screen appears.
  4. Tap Reset and confirm your action.

Once the reset process finishes, you can pair the watch again using the Watch app on iPhone. During the pairing process, you will be asked to choose a new passcode.

Remember, since the Apple Watch does not ask for the Apple Account password during the reset process, you’ll be required to enter it when pairing the watch again if Activation Lock is enabled.

How to Restore Apple Watch Data After Reset

During the Apple Watch pairing process, the Watch app offers you two options:

  • Restore from Backup.
  • Set Up as a New Apple Watch.

Choose the Restore from Backup option to bring back apps, settings, and watch faces. Health and Fitness data also returns if iCloud sync was enabled earlier.

Can You Reset Apple Watch Without Apple ID or Password?

No. If Activation Lock is active, the original Apple ID and password are mandatory during setup. This security feature prevents lost or stolen watches from being reused.

If you forgot your Apple ID credentials, recover them through Apple account recovery before proceeding.

Apple Watch Reset Not Working? Common Issues and Fixes

If you’re having trouble resetting or setting up your Apple Watch after forgetting the passcode, the following fixes should help you get back on track:

Tips to Avoid Forgetting Your Apple Watch Passcode Again

While forgetting your Apple Watch passcode is uncommon, it can still happen. Follow these simple habits to reduce the chances of getting locked out again.

  • Enable Unlock with iPhone, so your watch unlocks automatically when your iPhone is nearby.
  • Avoid changing your passcode frequently unless necessary.
  • Choose a passcode that’s secure but easy to remember.
  • Wear your Apple Watch regularly to keep passcode muscle memory intact.
  • Keep iCloud backups enabled to protect your data.
  • Store your Apple Account credentials securely in a trusted password manager.

Summing Up…

And that’s it. This is how you can reset your Apple Watch passcode and get your Apple Watch working again. Now you know that if your iPhone is nearby, unpairing through the Watch app is the fastest solution. If not, resetting directly from the watch still works as long as you have your Apple ID.

Did this guide help you reset your Apple Watch? Let us know in the comments.

title.rendered: How to Sync Google and Outlook Calendars on iPhone

content.rendered:
Managing appointments across multiple platforms can get messy quickly. One meeting lives in Google Calendar, another shows up in Microsoft Outlook, and suddenly your iPhone feels out of sync with real life. Luckily, you can pull everything into one place using the built-in Calendar app on your iPhone.

Once set up, your work meetings and personal plans sync automatically across all your Apple devices that are signed in with the same Apple Account. Keep reading to learn how to sync Google and Outlook calendars with your iPhone

Table of Contents
  • Why Sync Google and Outlook Calendars on Your iPhone
  • How to Sync Google Calendar with iPhone
    • Google Calendar Not Syncing on iPhone? Fixes to Try
  • How to Sync Outlook Calendar with iPhone
    • Outlook Calendar Not Showing on iPhone? How to Fix It
  • How to View Google and Outlook Calendars Together on iPhone
  • How to Set a Default Calendar on iPhone for New Events
  • Tips to Manage Multiple Calendars on iPhone More Efficiently
  • Bringing It All Together…

Why Sync Google and Outlook Calendars on Your iPhone

It is quite common for many of us to juggle at least two calendars. Google usually handles personal schedules while Outlook manages office meetings. Therefore, syncing both with your iPhone gives you benefits such as:

  • One unified daily view
  • Real-time updates across platforms
  • Fewer missed reminders
  • Easier planning on the go

After setup, any event you add or edit on your iPhone reflects back to Google or Outlook automatically.

How to Sync Google Calendar with iPhone

Syncing your Google Calendar brings all its events into the built-in Calendar app on your iPhone. Here’s how:

  1. Open Settings, scroll to the bottom, and tap Apps.
  2. Here, locate and tap Calendar.
  3. Tap Calendar Accounts.
  4. Now, tap Add Account.
  5. Select Google under “Choose your provider.”
  6. Tap the Open Browser button on the pop-up prompt that appears.
  7. Next, sign in to your Google account.
  8. Follow the onscreen instructions.
  9. Tap Save.

Google Calendar Not Syncing on iPhone? Fixes to Try

There are usually two reasons your events from Google Calendar are not showing up in the Calendar app on your iPhone.

Either the Calendar app does not have permission to access your calendar data, or Google calendars are turned off for your account on the device. Once both permissions are enabled, your events should sync normally across your Apple devices.

To check whether the Calendar app has permission to access your Google Calendar data:

  1. Go to Settings → Apps → Calendar.
    Tap Calendar Accounts.
  2. Tap Calendar Accounts → Google Account.
  3. Make sure the toggle next to Calendars is green.

To ensure Google Calendar isn’t turned off for your account on the device:

  1. Tap the Calendar icon in the Calendar app.
  2. Make sure all the boxes under your Google account are checked.

How to Sync Outlook Calendar with iPhone

Like the Google Calendar, syncing your Microsoft Outlook calendar to your iPhone brings all your work meetings and reminders into the built-in Calendar app. Here’s how:

  1. Go to Settings → Apps → Calendar.
  2. Tap Calendar Accounts → Add Account.
  3. Select Outlook.com under “Choose your provider.”
  4. Tap the Open Browser button.
  5. Next, sign in to your Outlook account and follow the onscreen instructions.
  6. Tap Save.

Outlook Calendar Not Showing on iPhone? How to Fix It

If events from Microsoft Outlook aren’t showing on your iPhone, the Calendar app may not have permission to access your data, or Outlook calendars might be turned off for your account. If you’re using an Exchange account, your admin may also need to enable mobile calendar sync.

Re-enable Calendars in iPhone Settings, then open the Calendar app and confirm all Outlook calendars are checked.

How to View Google and Outlook Calendars Together on iPhone

Once you have added both your Google and Outlook calendars to your iPhone, here’s how you can ensure events from both accounts appear in the Calendar app:

  1. Open the Calendar app and tap the Calendar icon at the bottom right corner.
  2. Here, make sure all the boxes under your Google and Outlook accounts are checked.
  3. Once done, tap the X button at the top left corner.

How to Set a Default Calendar on iPhone for New Events

To avoid new appointments landing in the wrong account, do this:

  1. Go to Settings → Apps → Calendar.
  2. Locate and tap Default Calendar.
  3. Choose Google or Outlook.

From now on, anything you create on your iPhone saves to the chosen calendar automatically.

Tips to Manage Multiple Calendars on iPhone More Efficiently

Now that you’ve synced your Google and Outlook calendars with your iPhone, these simple habits help keep everything organized across your Apple devices:

  • Use different colors for calendars from Google Calendar and Microsoft Outlook for quick visual sorting.
  • Set a default calendar on your iPhone so new events save to the right account.
  • Turn on notifications for all linked calendars to avoid missed reminders.
  • Review your upcoming week regularly to catch overlaps early.
  • Hide unused shared calendars to reduce clutter.
  • Create events directly on your iPhone so changes sync instantly across your Apple devices.

Bringing It All Together…

Syncing Google and Outlook calendars with your iPhone dramatically improves day-to-day planning. Once set up, your meetings, reminders, and personal events stay aligned without manual effort. It only takes a few minutes to set up, but it saves hours of back-and-forth later. With all your schedules in one place, you can focus more on your day and less on juggling apps.

Have a tip or run into an issue while setting this up on your iPhone? Let us know in the comments.

  • How to remove iPhone calendar virus (Tips to stop the spam)
  • Best Calendar Apps for iPhone

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A trusted iPhone, iPad, or Mac signed in to your Apple Account is required to create or update a recovery key.

mainEntity.name: What happens if I lose my Apple Recovery Key?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you still have access to a trusted device, you can generate a new key. If you lose both your trusted devices and your recovery key, your Apple Account may become permanently inaccessible.

mainEntity.name: Can I view my Apple Recovery Key again after I set it up?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Apple displays it only once during setup.

mainEntity.name: Where should I store my recovery key safely?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use a secure offline method such as: A written note stored in a safe place An encrypted USB drive A trusted password manager Avoid storing it in iCloud Photos, Notes, or iCloud Drive.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. One recovery key applies to every device signed in to your Apple Account.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: What is Tracking Notifications on iPhone: What You Need to Know

content.rendered:
Seeing “AirTag Found Moving With You” or “Unknown Accessory Detected Near You” means your iPhone detected a tracker that may be traveling with you.

It could be harmless (borrowed keys, a bag, a shared item). It could also be unwanted tracking. This article tells you what the alert means, why Apple added it, how it triggers, and what to do next.

Table of Contents
  • What are Tracking Notifications on iPhone?
  • How Tracking Notifications Work
  • What a Tracking Notification Looks Like
  • What to Do If You Receive a Tracking Notification on Your iPhone
    • 1. Locate the Device
    • 2. Check Device Information
    • 3. Pause Alerts If You Recognize the Device
    • 4. Disable the Device If It’s Unfamiliar
  • How to Turn On Tracking Notifications on iPhone
  • How to Turn Off Tracking Notifications (And Why You Shouldn't)
  • Common Issues and Helpful Tips
  • Why Tracking Notifications Matter

What are Tracking Notifications on iPhone?

Tracking notifications are safety alerts built into Apple’s Find My network. Their purpose is to warn you if a tracking device that doesn’t belong to you appears to be moving with you.

Apple introduced this feature with iOS 14.5 in response to real privacy and safety concerns. Before tracking notifications existed, it was possible for someone to hide a small tracker in a bag, car, or pocket and follow another person’s movements without their knowledge. That kind of tracking is dangerous, invasive, and often completely invisible.

Now, instead of being tracked silently, your iPhone makes tracking visible with notifications. 

Tracking notifications work by detecting unknown AirTags, AirPods, or other Find My-compatible devices that appear to be traveling with you over time. When your iPhone notices a pattern that suggests tracking, it sends you an alert. It is a clear signal that something may be wrong.

How Tracking Notifications Work

Your iPhone is constantly scanning nearby Bluetooth signals in the background. You don’t see it happening, and it doesn’t drain your battery in any noticeable way.

Here’s how the process usually works:

  • Your iPhone detects a nearby AirTag or Find My–compatible device
  • The device appears to be separated from its owner
  • Your iPhone notices that the device is traveling with you
  • After several hours (usually between 8 and 24 hours), you receive a tracking notification

The system is designed to avoid false alarms. Devices owned by people in your Family Sharing group are ignored, and brief contact with a tracker won’t trigger an alert. The notification only appears when there’s a pattern that suggests tracking.

What a Tracking Notification Looks Like

When a tracking notification appears, it looks like a normal iPhone alert. You might see messages such as:

  • “AirTag Found Moving With You”
  • “Unknown Accessory Detected Near You”

You’ll see it on your lock screen and inside the Notification Center. Tapping the alert opens the Find My app, where Apple walks you through the next steps.

What to Do If You Receive a Tracking Notification on Your iPhone

Getting one of these alerts can feel unsettling, but the most important thing is to stay calm. The notification doesn’t automatically mean someone is trying to harm you. It simply means something needs your attention.

Once you tap the alert, you’ll see tools that help you understand what’s happening.

1. Locate the Device

Your iPhone will show where the device was first detected and the route it followed with you. You’ll have options to:

  • Play a sound on the AirTag to help you find it
  • Use precision tracking to guide you toward it

This is especially helpful if the device is hidden inside a bag, jacket, or vehicle.

2. Check Device Information

You can scan the tracker by holding it near the top of your iPhone. This opens a page with details such as:

  • The device’s serial number
  • A partial phone number or blurred email of the owner
  • Whether the device is marked as lost

If it’s marked as lost, the owner may have left contact information so you can return it.

3. Pause Alerts If You Recognize the Device

Sometimes the explanation is harmless. Maybe you borrowed a friend’s bag or keys and forgot they had an AirTag attached.

In this case, you can choose Pause Safety Alerts for a day or longer. This stops repeated notifications while keeping the feature available when you need it again.

4. Disable the Device If It’s Unfamiliar

If you don’t recognize the device and feel uncomfortable, your iPhone provides instructions to disable it. This usually involves removing the battery so it can no longer report location.

If you’re concerned about your safety, Apple strongly recommends contacting local law enforcement. They can work with Apple using the device’s serial number if needed.

How to Turn On Tracking Notifications on iPhone

Tracking notifications are turned on by default, but it’s worth checking your settings to make sure everything is working properly.

First, your iPhone needs a few basics enabled:

  • Location Services must be on
  • Bluetooth must be on
  • Airplane Mode must be off
  • Find My must be active

To check or enable tracking notifications:

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap Notifications.
  3. Scroll to Tracking Notifications.
  4. Turn on Allow Notifications.

You can also find this option in the Find My app by tapping Me and selecting Customize Tracking Notifications.

How to Turn Off Tracking Notifications (And Why You Shouldn’t)

You can turn tracking notifications off, but Apple does not recommend it because it reduces your safety.

To turn them off:

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap Notifications.
  3. Scroll to Tracking Notifications.

This turns off the alerts, so your iPhone will stop warning you about unknown trackers that may be moving with you.

Most people are safer leaving tracking notifications enabled. They run quietly in the background and only appear when something unusual happens.

Common Issues and Helpful Tips

If you’re not receiving tracking notifications, make sure:

  • Your iPhone is running iOS 14.5 or later
  • Find My is enabled
  • Bluetooth and Location Services are turned on

False alerts can happen, especially with shared or borrowed items. The system improves over time and learns from your interactions.

Apple also adds extra protection by making AirTags play sounds after being separated from their owner for several days. This makes them harder to hide and easier to discover.

Why Tracking Notifications Matter

Tracking notifications are one of those features you hope you never need, but are grateful to have when you do.

They work silently, respect your privacy, and step in only when something doesn’t feel right. In a small notification, Apple gives users awareness, choice, and control.

In a world where personal safety and digital privacy are closely connected, tracking notifications are not just a setting. They are peace of mind.

Keeping them enabled is one of the simplest and smartest ways to protect yourself without changing how you use your iPhone at all.

FAQs

What is the difference between Tracking Notifications and App Tracking?

Tracking Notifications warn you about physical trackers like AirTags that may be moving with you. App Tracking controls whether apps can track your activity across other apps and websites for advertising.

Which devices can trigger Tracking Notifications?

Most alerts are for AirTags and other Find My compatible items, including some accessories like AirPods, when they appear to be traveling with you while separated from their owner.

How long does it take to get a tracking notification?

It is not instant. In many cases, you may get an alert after several hours, often around 8 to 24 hours of the device moving with you.

acceptedAnswer.text: Tracking Notifications warn you about physical trackers like AirTags that may be moving with you. App Tracking controls whether apps can track your activity across other apps and websites for advertising.

mainEntity.name: Which devices can trigger Tracking Notifications?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most alerts are for AirTags and other Find My compatible items, including some accessories like AirPods, when they appear to be traveling with you while separated from their owner.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to get a tracking notification?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is not instant. In many cases, you may get an alert after several hours, often around 8 to 24 hours of the device moving with you.

title.rendered: iOS 27 Will Focus on Stability and Refinement Rather Than Major New Features

content.rendered:
Apple is preparing to present iOS 27 at the 2026 Worldwide Developers Conference, and early reports suggest the update will be more restrained than in past years. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, the next version of iOS will emphasize bug fixes, performance improvements, and small design refinements instead of introducing major new features.

This approach suggests Apple is placing greater importance on usability and reliability, potentially addressing issues that have accumulated as the platform has grown more complex.

Siri Is Expected to Receive a More Personalized, Chatbot-Style Experience

The most significant change in iOS 27 is expected to involve Siri. Apple is reportedly working on a more personalized version of the assistant that uses a chatbot-style interface as part of its Apple Intelligence efforts.

While the Siri update is seen as a meaningful step forward, it is not expected to fundamentally change the rest of the operating system. Instead, it will likely stand out as the primary new feature in an otherwise refinement-focused release.

Performance Improvements and Bug Fixes Are Expected to Take Priority

iOS 27 is expected to focus on making the system feel faster, smoother, and more reliable. Apple is reportedly targeting long-standing bugs, optimizing performance, and making subtle visual adjustments rather than adding new system-wide capabilities.

Although these changes may not be highly visible during a keynote presentation, they can significantly improve the everyday experience for users.

Early Siri Improvements Are Expected to Appear in iOS 26.4

Ahead of the iOS 27 preview, Apple is expected to release the first developer beta of iOS 26.4 during the week of February 23. This update is said to include some early components of the planned Siri improvements.

Releasing these changes ahead of WWDC would give developers additional time to test and prepare for Apple’s longer-term plans.

WWDC 2026 Is Expected to Take Place in Early June

Apple is likely to announce WWDC 2026 toward the end of March, with the event expected to take place in the first or second week of June. As in previous years, beta versions of Apple’s new software are expected to be available to developers shortly after the keynote, with a public release planned for the fall.

If accurate, iOS 27 may stand out less for new features and more for how it improves the overall stability and polish of the iPhone experience.

mainEntity.name: Does Facebook have a cache?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Facebook uses app cache, media cache, and in-app browser cache to store temporary data.

mainEntity.name: How often should I clear my Facebook cache?

acceptedAnswer.text: Active users should clear the cache every 1–2 weeks. Moderate users can clear it once a month or whenever the app feels slow.

mainEntity.name: Can clearing the cache fix Facebook not loading images or videos?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Corrupted or outdated cache files often cause media loading issues. Clearing the cache usually resolves the problem.

mainEntity.name: Why does my iPhone show a signal but no internet?

acceptedAnswer.text: This usually means your phone is connected to the cellular network but cannot access mobile data. Common causes include disabled cellular data, an expired data plan, incorrect network settings, or carrier provisioning issues.

mainEntity.name: Why is my mobile data not working while on a call on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some networks do not support simultaneous voice and data connections. Enabling VoLTE, if supported by your carrier, usually fixes this issue.

mainEntity.name: How to fix 5G not working on your iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Make sure you have an active 5G plan and that 5G is enabled in Settings > Cellular > Cellular Data Options > Voice & Data. Also, ensure you are in a 5G coverage area and that your carrier supports 5G on your device.

mainEntity.name: Why is LTE or 3G not working on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many carriers are shutting down 3G networks as LTE and 4G become standard. If you use an older iPhone that only supports 3G, you may need to upgrade to a newer model that supports LTE or 4G.

mainEntity.name: Can Apple Pay be used if the iPhone is locked?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Apple Pay requires authentication through Face ID, Touch ID, or the device passcode. Without this verification, payments cannot be completed.

mainEntity.name: Does disabling Apple Pay cancel your physical cards?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Disabling Apple Pay only removes the card from the lost device. Your physical debit or credit cards remain active unless you cancel them through your bank.

mainEntity.name: How do I disable Apple Pay remotely without my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can disable Apple Pay remotely by signing into iCloud Find Devices, selecting your device, and enabling Lost Mode. This suspends Apple Pay cards immediately.

acceptedAnswer.text: Most users only need 10–15 essential apps. Installing too many apps can clutter the interface and reduce battery efficiency. Focus on apps you use daily.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Apps downloaded from the App Store generally follow Apple’s privacy and security guidelines. However, always check permissions, developer reputation, and reviews before installing health or tracking apps.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a trusted device to set up a recovery key?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A trusted iPhone, iPad, or Mac signed in to your Apple Account is required to create or update a recovery key.

mainEntity.name: What happens if I lose my Apple Recovery Key?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you still have access to a trusted device, you can generate a new key. If you lose both your trusted devices and your recovery key, your Apple Account may become permanently inaccessible.

mainEntity.name: Can I view my Apple Recovery Key again after I set it up?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Apple displays it only once during setup.

mainEntity.name: Where should I store my recovery key safely?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use a secure offline method such as: A written note stored in a safe place An encrypted USB drive A trusted password manager Avoid storing it in iCloud Photos, Notes, or iCloud Drive.

mainEntity.name: Can one recovery key work across all devices?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. One recovery key applies to every device signed in to your Apple Account.

mainEntity.name: Is a recovery key required for Advanced Data Protection?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not specifically. However, you must choose at least one recovery method, either a Recovery Key or a Recovery Contact, to enable Advanced Data Protection.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between Tracking Notifications and App Tracking?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tracking Notifications warn you about physical trackers like AirTags that may be moving with you. App Tracking controls whether apps can track your activity across other apps and websites for advertising.

mainEntity.name: Which devices can trigger Tracking Notifications?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most alerts are for AirTags and other Find My compatible items, including some accessories like AirPods, when they appear to be traveling with you while separated from their owner.
